title: Rewards, Regrets, and Rubber Arms: A Historical Development Review of Reinforcement Learning in Games and Robotics
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Reinforcement Learning in Games and Robotics in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of reinforcement learning and robotics as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: Dataset Evaluasi Kinerja Model Representasi Teks (S-BERT, TF-IDF, Word2Vec) pada Chatbot Sejarah Kalimantan Tengah: Uji Ketahanan terhadap Variasi Bahasa Informal, Typo, dan Parafrase
abstract: Dataset berisi hasil evaluasi komprehensif terhadap kinerja model representasi teks (Sentence-BERT, TF-IDF, dan Word2Vec) yang dikombinasikan dengan filter klasifikasi intent SVM dan Cosine Similarity untuk sistem chatbot edukasi sejarah Kalimantan Tengah. Data mencakup skor similaritas, jawaban Knowledge Base, dan label kecocokan pertanyaan prediksi dengan pertanyaan aslinya (Sesuai/Tidak Sesuai) dari berbagai skenario pengujian ketahanan model, meliputi variasi typo ringan, bahasa informal/singkatan, serta berbagai jenis transformasi parafrase linguistik. Dataset ini bertujuan untuk mendukung penelitian Natural Language Processing (NLP) dalam menangani input pengguna bahasa Indonesia yang tidak baku.

title: Quantum Adaptive Geometry Model
abstract: Quantum Adaptive Geometry Model explores the potential of utilizing quantum entanglement and self-adaptive mechanisms to revolutionize computational efficiency and precision. This research focuses on designing a quantum-based geometry model capable of automated geometric transformation optimization. The core claim posits that this model, through the combined effects of quantum entanglement and self-adaptation, will significantly enhance computational capabilities. This paper details the theoretical framework, proposed algorithm, and initial experimental results demonstrating the model's capability to adjust geometric transformations with minimal computational overhead. We will discuss the underlying mathematical principles and potential applications of this approach, emphasizing the benefits of quantum mechanics for geometric optimization.

title: Title: Adaptive Topological Quantum State Conjugation
abstract: Adaptive topological quantum state conjugation represents a paradigm shift in quantum state manipulation, offering unprecedented control and responsiveness compared to traditional methods. This paper introduces a novel approach that leverages the inherent properties of self-adjoint topological structures to dynamically conjugate quantum states. We detail the core mechanism, outlining the process of constructing and utilizing these structures to achieve precise and controllable state evolution. The resulting method promises significant advancements in quantum information processing and quantum systems, particularly in the realm of dynamic control and superposition manipulation. The key innovation lies in the ability to establish and maintain a complex, self-consistent topological structure that governs the state's evolution, effectively bridging the gap between classical and quantum states. This results in a more robust and adaptable framework for manipulating quantum states. The study presents a comprehensive analysis of the algorithm's performance and potential applications across diverse quantum systems, highlighting the advantages offered by this adaptive topology approach. The paper concludes with a discussion of future research directions and potential implications for the future of quantum technology.

The core mechanism centers around leveraging quantum entanglement for computation, aiming to surpass the limitations of classical computing. The investigation will delve into the potential applications of PMM within quantum computing, focusing on its ability to enhance calculation accuracy and efficiency. This paper aims to provide a comprehensive overview of the theoretical groundwork, explore preliminary computational strategies, and outline future research directions. The significance of this work lies in the potential to revolutionize numerical simulations and computational modeling, particularly within the realm of quantum physics.

title: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning with Contract Nets for Cooperative Task Allocation
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to cooperative multi-agent task allocation using Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) and a mechanism leveraging Contract Nets. The core idea is that agents learn to execute specific tasks – represented as "contracts" – each with associated rewards, and utilize Contract Nets to facilitate negotiation and coordination. Traditional MARL struggles with scalability and achieving robust cooperation in complex, dynamic environments due to the non-stationary nature of the environment from each agent's perspective. Contract Nets provide a structured way to represent and reason about task assignments, allowing agents to dynamically adapt to changes and effectively coordinate towards a shared goal. We demonstrate the efficacy of this approach through theoretical analysis and conceptual outlining, highlighting the potential for improved task allocation and overall system performance compared to standard MARL techniques. The key contribution lies in the integration of Contract Nets within the MARL framework, offering a scalable and adaptable solution for cooperative problem-solving.

title: Quantum Entanglement Synchronization Networks
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, promises revolutionary advancements in secure communication and accelerated computation. However, maintaining entanglement over significant distances presents a formidable challenge due to environmental noise and decoherence. This paper explores a novel network architecture, Quantum Entanglement Synchronization Networks (QENS), designed to address these challenges through dynamic synchronization, adaptive weighting, and feedback loops. We propose a system that actively monitors and adjusts the entanglement state, mitigating decoherence and enabling long-distance communication with enhanced fidelity. The core mechanism centers on a dynamically evolving entanglement weighting matrix, optimizing for coherence preservation and information amplification. This approach offers a substantial improvement over existing approaches, particularly in the context of long-range synchronization and robustness. The potential applications of QENS are wide-ranging, from quantum key distribution to distributed quantum computation.

title: Physical Simulation of Quantum Entanglement Parameters for Quantum Key Distribution Optimization
abstract: Quantum entanglement is a fundamental phenomenon in quantum mechanics with immense potential for secure communication and computation. Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) leverages entanglement to establish a secure key between two parties, offering unparalleled security. However, practical implementation of QKD faces challenges related to entanglement management and error correction. This paper explores a novel approach to QKD optimization using physical simulation, specifically focusing on dynamically adjusting entanglement parameters to enhance key distribution efficiency. We propose a framework that leverages the unique properties of entangled states to guide the optimization process, providing a more robust and adaptable method compared to traditional classical approaches. The core mechanism involves employing a quantum simulator to model entangled states and iteratively refine parameters, ultimately leading to improved key distribution performance. The study demonstrates the effectiveness of this approach through simulations and provides insights into potential improvements for future QKD systems.

abstract: This paper presents Beatrix's Bat, a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of bats. title: Beady-eyed Mouse: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Visual Perception of Mice
abstract: This paper presents Beady-eyed Mouse, a new metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the visual perception strategies employed by mice. Mice utilize a sophisticated system of eye movements and attentional shifts to efficiently scan their environment, identifying salient features and potential food sources. Beady-eyed Mouse mimics this process by incorporating a dynamic focus of attention, a probabilistic exploration strategy, and a local search mechanism. The algorithm's core components include a focus vector, a movement strategy based on visual saliency, and a penalty function to discourage convergence to local optima. We evaluate Beady-eyed Mouse on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Simulated Annealing (SA). The key metrics used for evaluation include convergence rate, solution quality, and computational complexity. The results indicate that Beady-eyed Mouse offers a robust and efficient approach to solving complex optimization problems, particularly those with high dimensionality and multimodal landscapes. Finally, we discuss future research directions, including incorporating adaptive parameters based on environmental complexity and exploring hybrid approaches combining Beady-eyed Mouse with other optimization techniques.

title: Formal Verification of Secure Multi-Party Computation using Abstract Interpretation
abstract: Secure Multi-Party Computation (SMPC) enables computations on sensitive data without revealing the data itself to any participant. However, ensuring the security and correctness of SMPC protocols is a significant challenge, primarily due to their intricate designs and reliance on often-assumed cryptographic properties. This work introduces a novel approach to SMPC verification using abstract interpretation. We transform the complex protocol into a higher-level abstract representation, facilitating the application of abstract interpretation algorithms to detect potential vulnerabilities related to protocol soundness, privacy, and correctness. The proposed methodology offers a more scalable and robust verification framework compared to traditional methods, addressing a critical bottleneck in the deployment of secure distributed computation systems. Our approach leverages abstract domains to approximate the protocol's behavior, allowing for efficient analysis of complex interactions and the identification of subtle errors that might otherwise go unnoticed. This research provides a theoretical foundation and a practical framework for verifying SMPC protocols, ultimately contributing to increased trust and security in distributed computing environments.

title: ## Bahaman Funnel-eared Bat Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the "Bahaman Funnel-eared Bat" (BFB) algorithm, inspired by the foraging behavior of the Bahaman funnel-eared bat ( *Natalus noctivagus* ). These bats utilize a unique funnel-shaped movement strategy to efficiently search for food in complex environments. The algorithm leverages this strategy by employing a dynamic exploration-exploitation balance, mimicking the bat's oscillating movement patterns and adaptation to varying resource densities. The BFB algorithm incorporates key features such as a population-based search, a dynamic movement radius, and an adaptive learning rate mechanism. We demonstrate the algorithm's effectiveness on several benchmark optimization problems, including the Rosenbrock function, the Rastrigin function, and the Sphere function. Results indicate that the BFB algorithm exhibits competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic techniques like the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and the Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) algorithm, particularly in challenging, high-dimensional landscapes. The algorithm's performance analysis highlights its adaptability and robustness, suggesting its potential for application in diverse complex optimization scenarios. Future research directions include exploring hybrid approaches combining the BFB algorithm with other optimization techniques and its application to real-world engineering problems.

title: Towards a Universal Computing Architecture Based on Quantum Coherence Degradation
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to universal computation leveraging the precise control of quantum coherence degradation, often considered a detrimental effect in quantum computing. Instead of mitigating decoherence, we argue for its utilization as a fundamental resource. The core idea revolves around designing quantum circuits that exploit specific noise patterns to achieve precise control and manipulation of qubits. This architecture, termed the "Quantum Noise-Based Universal Computing Architecture," fundamentally shifts the paradigm by recognizing and harnessing the inherent variability introduced by quantum systems. We outline the theoretical framework, detailing the core mechanism which relies on carefully engineered circuits to orchestrate controlled decoherence, ultimately enabling universal computation. This approach circumvents the limitations inherent in traditional quantum computing methods that primarily focus on suppressing decoherence. The proposed architecture offers a pathway toward scalable and potentially more robust quantum computation.

title: Atalaya Nesophontes: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Fossilized Camelid
abstract: This paper introduces Atalaya Nesophontes (AN), a novel metaheuristic algorithm designed to address complex optimization problems. The algorithm's inspiration stems from the fossilized camelid, *Atalaya nesophontes*, known for its remarkable resilience and adaptive survival strategies in harsh environments. AN combines elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Simulated Annealing (SA) with a unique adaptive mechanism based on population density and historical solution quality. The core of AN lies in its 'Adaptive Mutation Rate' (AMR) and 'Dynamic Neighborhood Structure' (DNS) mechanisms. AMR dynamically adjusts the mutation rate based on the population's convergence behavior, preventing premature convergence. DNS modifies the neighborhood structure of the search space, favoring exploration in regions with high population density and exploiting promising solutions in areas with a history of successful discoveries. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and efficiency compared to established metaheuristic algorithms. The results show that AN consistently achieves good solutions with a relatively low computational cost, highlighting its potential for practical applications. This paper presents the algorithm's theoretical foundation, implementation details, and empirical results, contributing a new approach to the field of metaheuristic optimization.

abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed Aoudad-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (AIMA), motivated by the foraging behavior of the Aoudad ( *Aoudad capra* ), a resilient desert antelope. The Aoudad's efficient navigation and resource exploitation strategies in challenging environments inspire the algorithm's design. AIMA leverages a dynamic territory system and a weighted exploration-exploitation mechanism, mimicking the Aoudad's territorial defense and resource selection. The algorithm incorporates a novel adaptive parameter control scheme based on a simulated "herd pressure" to regulate the search process. The core of AIMA lies in its territory allocation strategy, where particles compete for territories, and the probability of territory acquisition is influenced by a combination of particle fitness and a random factor. Furthermore, the algorithm employs a weighted average of particle velocities to encourage exploration and exploitation. Theoretical analysis focuses on the algorithm's convergence properties and computational complexity. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic methods. The results showcase AIMA's potential as a robust and efficient solution for various complex optimization challenges.

title: Polar Rat Optimization Algorithm (PROA): A Novel Metaheuristic for Complex Problem Solving
abstract: This paper introduces the Polar Rat Optimization Algorithm (PROA), a new metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of Arctic ground squirrels (Lemmus polaris). PROA leverages the principles of directional movement, territory exploration, and adaptive polarization to efficiently navigate complex search spaces. The algorithm utilizes a population of "rats" (candidate solutions) that move through a defined space, guided by a polarization vector and a directional vector. The polarization vector represents the overall trend of the population, while the directional vector dictates individual movement. Key parameters, including polarization strength, directional bias, and exploration frequency, are dynamically adjusted based on the algorithm's performance and the characteristics of the problem being solved. PROA aims to provide a robust and adaptable solution for optimization problems exhibiting high dimensionality, non-convexity, and multimodal landscapes. This paper outlines the algorithm's core mechanics, provides a theoretical framework, and discusses potential applications.

title: Causal Inference Based on Multi-Modal Latent Variables
abstract: This paper addresses the limitations of traditional causal inference methods that often rely solely on single-modal observational data, neglecting the intricate interactions between modalities and leading to biased inference results. We propose a novel approach utilizing multi-modal latent variables to enhance causal inference. This method maps diverse observational data into a shared latent variable space, leveraging graph models and Bayesian networks for precise causal relationship discovery. The core of our method lies in the explicit modeling of complex interactions between modalities through these hidden variables. We demonstrate the potential of this framework to improve causal understanding in scenarios with rich, multi-modal data. The key contributions include a formalization of the multi-modal latent variable framework and a methodology for causal inference that accounts for modality-specific confounders and interactions. ---

title: Quantum-Enhanced Wave Function Collapse for Quantum Machine Learning
abstract: Quantum machine learning (QML) holds immense promise for revolutionizing fields ranging from drug discovery to materials science. However, the computational complexity of many QML algorithms, particularly those involving complex systems, presents a significant bottleneck. This paper explores a novel approach leveraging quantum entanglement and superposition to accelerate the collapse of wave functions, thereby substantially improving the efficiency of quantum machine learning algorithms. We propose a new quantum algorithm, termed "Quantum Collapse Acceleration Protocol" (QCAP), designed to mitigate the computational burden associated with wave function collapse, a crucial step in many QML processes. The core mechanism of QCAP involves carefully orchestrated entanglement and superposition manipulations to guide the algorithm towards a quicker and more stable state of quantum information. This leads to reduced computational time and improved performance for specific QML tasks. The proposed algorithm demonstrates potential for significant speedups compared to classical approaches, offering a pathway towards more practical and scalable quantum machine learning.

title: Adaptive Graph Embedding with Relational Context
abstract: Graph embedding techniques have become increasingly prevalent in various domains, including social network analysis, recommendation systems, and knowledge graph reasoning. However, traditional graph embedding methods often treat nodes and edges independently, neglecting the crucial relational context that governs the structure of the graph. This paper introduces an adaptive graph embedding method designed to address this limitation. The core idea is to learn embeddings by explicitly incorporating the relationships between nodes, leveraging the contextual information surrounding each connection. We employ a recurrent neural network (RNN) to process this relational context, generating embeddings that are sensitive to these contextual dependencies. The resulting embeddings are expected to provide more accurate and informative representations of nodes compared to methods that disregard relational context. This work demonstrates the potential of incorporating contextual information into graph embedding, leading to improved performance across a range of graph-based tasks.

title: Dimensional Low Coupling Quantum Error Correction
abstract: Quantum error correction (QEC) is a critical component of quantum computing, enabling the reliable manipulation of quantum information. However, current QEC schemes often rely on a fixed number of qubits, limiting their scalability and error correction capabilities. This paper proposes a novel approach to QEC based on dynamically adjusting the dimensionality of the quantum state. We introduce a "quantum topology state" mechanism that leverages the unique properties of quantum error correction to dynamically control and optimize the quantum state, thereby significantly reducing quantum error rates. This design offers a pathway towards higher precision and improved error correction performance, addressing a critical limitation of existing QEC techniques.

title: ## Angolan Dormouse Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Dormouse Search (DS)," inspired by the foraging behavior of Angolan Dormice ( *Graphomys dasytonotus*). Dormice are renowned for their efficient and adaptive foraging strategies, particularly their ability to rapidly locate food sources in complex environments. DS leverages this observed behavior to develop a new optimization technique. The algorithm employs a population-based search strategy, utilizing a "nest" representation to simulate the dormouse's caching behavior, and incorporates a novel adaptation mechanism based on the concept of "probe zones" to enhance exploration. The core components of DS include a nest construction mechanism, a probe zone generation and adjustment procedure, and an adaptive probability assignment scheme. We demonstrate the effectiveness of DS through theoretical analysis and simulations on several benchmark optimization problems, including the Rosenbrock function, Rastrigin function, and the Sphere function. The results indicate that DS exhibits competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms like Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), particularly in challenging, high-dimensional landscapes. The algorithm's key innovations lie in its ability to balance exploration and exploitation effectively, leading to faster convergence and improved solution quality. Future research will focus on extending DS to handle multi-objective optimization and real-world engineering applications.

title: Title: Geometric Group Theory for Cryptography
abstract: Geometric group theory offers a promising approach to cryptography by leveraging the inherent structure of geometric objects and transformations. This paper explores the application of this theory to key generation, focusing on designing keys resistant to established attacks through the manipulation of geometric group operations. We propose a novel framework that formalizes the relationship between cryptographic algorithms and geometric group operations, aiming to create keys with inherent security guarantees. The core mechanism involves rigorously analyzing the group structure of cryptographic primitives and applying geometric transformations to produce keys with enhanced resistance to known attacks. This research aims to provide a mathematically grounded approach to key generation, potentially simplifying the design process and enhancing the security of cryptographic systems. The study highlights the potential benefits of this geometric framework compared to traditional methods, emphasizing the robustness derived from geometric transformations.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Bayesian Network Propagation for Risk Assessment
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of quantum computing to enhance Bayesian Network (BN) propagation for risk assessment. Traditional BN models struggle with scalability and computational complexity, particularly when dealing with long-time horizons and complex scenarios. We propose a novel framework that leverages quantum algorithms to accelerate probabilistic model updates, thereby improving accuracy and enabling more sophisticated risk assessment. This work explores the feasibility of quantum-enhanced BN propagation through the application of variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) and quantum annealing techniques. The core claim is that quantum computing offers a significant advantage in risk assessment by improving model accuracy and providing a more robust representation of uncertainty.

title: Optimization Algorithms Based on Graph Theory for Quantum Computing
abstract: Quantum computing offers the potential for revolutionary advancements across diverse fields, demanding efficient algorithms and hardware architectures. Traditional optimization methods often overlook the inherent structural properties of quantum circuits, hindering their potential for optimal performance. This paper proposes a novel optimization algorithm based on graph theory, designed to leverage the structural characteristics of quantum circuits to enhance efficiency. The core mechanism involves representing quantum circuits as graphs, utilizing graph properties to guide the optimization process. We explore the application of this approach to optimize quantum circuit parameters, focusing on minimizing circuit depth and improving fidelity. The paper details the algorithm's architecture, the mathematical underpinnings of its optimization strategy, and preliminary results demonstrating its effectiveness in optimizing quantum circuits. The research highlights the potential of graph-based optimization to accelerate the development of practical quantum algorithms.

title: Geometric Quantum State Representation with Adaptive Density
abstract: This paper introduces a novel geometric representation of quantum states, termed "Geometric Quantum State Representation with Adaptive Density," designed to capture and leverage quantum information more effectively. Traditional representations often lack the ability to dynamically adapt to subtle variations in the quantum state, hindering optimal information processing. We propose a system that utilizes a geometric density adaptation algorithm, which adjusts the representation's density based on observed quantum states, offering a dynamic and adaptable framework for quantum state analysis. The core mechanism centers on the intelligent mapping of quantum states onto a geometric space, enhancing information capture and potentially enabling new functionalities. This paper details the algorithmic design, discusses the theoretical foundations, and presents preliminary results demonstrating the superior performance of this representation compared to static representations.

title: 基于动态的随机矩阵的量子计算优化
abstract: Quantum computing has emerged as a transformative technology with the potential to revolutionize various fields, from drug discovery to materials science. However, efficient quantum algorithms and hardware are crucial for realizing this potential. Quantum computation is inherently sensitive to noise and requires careful optimization to achieve optimal performance. This paper explores a novel quantum computing optimization approach based on dynamically generated random matrices. We propose a framework where the quantum state is continuously perturbed by a dynamically changing set of random matrices, allowing for adaptive parameter adjustments and improved performance. The core mechanism centers around the iterative refinement of quantum states through this dynamic adjustment process. We analyze the impact of this approach on various quantum algorithms, demonstrating its potential to enhance computational efficiency and robustness. This work presents a promising direction for future research and development in quantum computing optimization.

title: African Trident Bat Algorithm for Multi-Objective Optimization
abstract: This paper presents the African Trident Bat Algorithm (ATBA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of African trident bats. The ATBA incorporates key characteristics of bat echolocation and social interaction, including frequency modulation, phase angle adjustment, and a dynamic exploration-exploitation balance. The algorithm utilizes a population-based approach, where each bat represents a potential solution. The algorithm's core components involve a dynamic frequency modulation scheme to represent the solution space, an adaptive phase angle adjustment mechanism to guide the search towards promising regions, and a social interaction model mimicking the bats' cooperative hunting strategy. The performance of the ATBA is evaluated on a range of benchmark multi-objective optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and competitiveness against established algorithms such as NSGA-II and MOEA/D. The algorithm's key parameters – the frequency modulation rate, phase angle adjustment factor, and social interaction strength – are dynamically adjusted based on the algorithm's convergence behavior, further enhancing its adaptability and performance. The results indicate that ATBA possesses strong capabilities in tackling complex multi-objective optimization problems, offering a robust and efficient alternative to existing metaheuristic methods. The algorithm's ability to effectively balance exploration and exploitation, combined with its dynamic adjustment mechanisms, contributes to its superior performance across diverse problem landscapes. The study highlights the potential of bio-inspired algorithms, particularly those drawing inspiration from animal behavior, for developing powerful optimization solutions.

title: أثر استخدام الذكاء الاصطناعي على نظم الحجز في قطاع السياحة في مصر (دراسة تطبيقية على عملاء مكاتب السياحة في القاهرة)
abstract: هدفت الدراسة إلى التعرف على أثر استخدام تقنيات الذكاء الاصطناعي على نظم الحجز في قطاع السياحة من وجهة نظر العملاء، مع دراسة تأثير متغيرات العمر والمستوى الدراسي والدخل. اعتمدت الدراسة على المنهجين الوصفي والتحليلي، حيث تم توزيع استبانة إلكترونية على عملاء مكاتب السياحة في مدينة القاهرة، وتم استرجاع 337 استبانة بنسبة 87.8%، وتم تحليل البيانات باستخدام برنامج SPSS من خلال الإحصاءات الوصفية والانحدار الخطي المتعدد واختبارات الارتباط والتعددية (VIF وTolerance). أظهرت النتائج ارتفاع مستوى اهتمام العملاء بالذكاء الاصطناعي ونظم الحجز، كما بينت أن جميع أبعاد الذكاء الاصطناعي، بما في ذلك النظم الخبيرة، الخوارزميات الجينية، تمثيل المعرفة والاستدلال، التعلم العميق، والروبوتات، لها أثر ذو دلالة إحصائية على نظم الحجز في قطاع السياحة. وبناءً على النتائج، أوصت الدراسة بتطوير نظم خبيرة لتقديم استشارات دقيقة وفورية للعملاء، ودمج تقنيات الذكاء الاصطناعي في البنية التحتية للحجز لتحسين رحلة العميل وجودة الخدمة، بالإضافة إلى استخدام الخوارزميات الجينية لإنشاء برامج رحلات مخصصة ومتوازنة بين التكلفة والوقت وشركات الطيران

title: Verbundprojekt: Rauscharme Laser für Quantenschlüsselaustausch mit kontinuierlichen Variablen - QuNET+LORELAY
abstract: Das Gesamtziel des Verbundprojekts ist die Entwicklung kompakter, Schrotrausch-limitierter Lasermodule mit geringer optischer Linienbreite einschließlich Betriebs- und Kontrollelektronik sowie geeigneter Fertigungstechnik für eine automatisierte Produktion in Europa. Damit sollen die Nachteile heutiger kommerzieller bzw. la-borbasierter Lasersysteme hinsichtlich CV-QKD-Eignung, Größe, Kosten und Leistungsaufnahme überwunden werden. Diese Laser sollen erst als Subsystem verifiziert und charakterisiert werden und dann in ein CV-QKD-System integriert werden. Ziel des Teilvorhabens der Adva Network Security GmbH (ANS) war die Definition geeigneter Laserspezifikationen und die Entwicklung einer Steuerelektronik aus diskreten Bauteilen, um Reichweite und Schlüsselrate faserbasierter CV-QKD-Systeme zu maximieren. Hierzu sollten insbesondere die Anforderungen an optische Ausgangsleistung, Linienbreite, Wellenlängenstabilität, Temperaturstabilisierung sowie die präzise Ansteuerung der verschiedenen Laserbereiche spezifiziert und in ein geeignetes elektronisches Ansteuerkonzept überführt werden. Die zu entwickelnde Elektronik sollte einen stabilen und möglichst rauscharmen Betrieb des Lasers ermöglichen sowie die gezielte Einstellung von Gain-, Phasen- und Tuningparametern unterstützen. Ein weiteres Ziel bestand darin, die entwickelte Hardware und Steuerungssoftware schrittweise mit realen Lasermodulen zu erproben und die Eignung des Gesamtsystems für den späteren Einsatz in CV-QKD-Anwendungen zu bewerten. Neben der reinen Ansteuerung sollten insbesondere die Temperaturregelung, die Wellenlängenabstimmung und das Zusammenspiel der einzelnen elektronischen Funktionsgruppen experimentell validiert werden. title: A Novel Fixed-Time Zeroing Neural Network for Real-Time Inter-Vehicle Distance Estimation in Autonomous Driving
abstract: Autonomous driving technology imposes stringent requirements on real-time environmental perception and dynamic distance measurement, which are critical prerequisites for vehicle path planning and driving safety. Traditional ranging methods relying on LiDAR and visual sensors often suffer from poor real-time performance and insufficient robustness in complex and dynamic traffic scenarios. To address this limitation, this paper proposes a novel fixed-time zeroing neural network (ZNN) to achieve high-precision and real-time inter-vehicle distance estimation for autonomous vehicles. First, a time-varying optimization model for inter-vehicle distance calculation is established based on dynamic programming theory, which fully considers the motion trajectories and structural constraints of adjacent vehicles. Subsequently, a dedicated activation function is designed to construct the improved fixed-time ZNN model for solving the above time-varying optimization problem. Rigorous theoretical proofs are presented to verify the fixed-time stability of the proposed network, and a tight upper bound of the convergence time is analytically derived. Moreover, comprehensive parameter selection strategies are discussed to guide practical model deployment. Finally, numerical simulation results demonstrate that the developed ZNN model possesses faster convergence speed and stronger robustness compared with existing methods, and it can accurately complete real-time distance calculation within a fixed time upper bound. The proposed method provides a new effective solution for dynamic ranging tasks in autonomous driving systems.

title: Multi-Target Tracking with HRRP-Aided Classification for Space-Based Radar Networks: An Enhanced Hybrid MF-BP Approach
abstract: Data association for space-based radar multi-target tracking is a significant challenge in dense clutter and complex scenarios, often leading to tracking errors and target loss. This paper proposes a classification-aided message-passing algorithm for space-based radars (CA-MP-SBRs), which employs a hybrid mean-field and belief-propagation (MF-BP) framework enhanced with target classification information. We leverage high-resolution range profile (HRRP) data, which are processed by a convolutional neural network (CNN) to classify targets. The classification output is then seamlessly integrated into the MF-BP framework to jointly infer target kinematic states, visibility states, data association, and class index. Simulation results demonstrate that incorporating HRRP-based classification improves data-association reliability and tracking accuracy. Specifically, compared with Classification-aided Gaussian mixture probability hypothesis density (CA-GM-PHD), the proposed CA-MP-SBRs reduces the average root mean square error (RMSE), optimal subpattern assignment (OSPA), and generalized optimal subpattern assignment (GOSPA) by 33.4%, 31.7%, and 32.1%, respectively, while the corresponding reductions relative to classification-aided labeled multi-Bernoulli tracking for space-based radars (CA-LMB-SBRs) are 23.2%, 25.6%, and 30.3%. These results confirm the effectiveness of CA-MP-SBRs for tracking diverse target types in dense-target scenarios.

title: UAV formation control for multi-target tracking based on an improved multi-agent double soft actor–critic
abstract: In recent years, formation control strategies based on multi-agent deep reinforcement learning (MADRL) have shown great potential for coordinating unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) in multi-target tracking (MTT) tasks. However, in complex, high-dimensional decision-making environments, the value evaluation networks in MADRL are prone to overestimation bias, undermining the stability of policy learning. Meanwhile, the risk of collisions among UAVs and uneven spatial distribution further limit the coordination efficiency and tracking performance of multi-UAV systems. To address these challenges, an improved multi-agent double soft actor–critic (i-MADSAC) framework is proposed for cooperative MTT tasks. Specifically, a centralized double-critic network based on an attention mechanism is developed to reduce variance and adapt to varying input dimensions by optimizing the double-critic network. Then, a distance-based inverse-square repulsion function is designed to effectively mitigate collision risks. In addition, a spatial information-entropy-based reward function is designed to optimize the spatial distribution and coverage of UAVs. It works in conjunction with the repulsion function to ensure efficient collision avoidance. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed i-MADSAC exhibits superior robustness, scalability, and tracking performance as the number of UAVs and task complexity increase, providing an efficient and reliable solution for MTT applications.

title: Federated learning explainable deep learning framework for enhanced internet of medical things security
abstract: The Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) enables remote patient monitoring, providing timely diagnostic assessments crucial for saving lives. Despite these benefits, IoMT systems face significant security challenges that endanger patient privacy and data integrity. Existing centralized machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) solutions, while useful, are “black boxes” that raise critical concerns about data privacy and ethical compliance, as sharing sensitive patient information in a centralized system may violate confidentiality, integrity, and availability, particularly in healthcare sectors where patient data is highly confidential. Motivated by these challenges, we propose a novel federated learning (FL) explainable deep recurrent neural network (DRNN)-augmented long short-term memory (LSTM) framework for anomaly intrusion in IoMT systems, named federated recurrent short-term memory. The proposed decentralized framework processes data on local devices, sharing only learned model weights with the central server to safeguard data integrity. Training the DRNN-LSTM presents a non-convex optimization problem that is computationally expensive. To address this issue, we propose a new Bayesian Optimization (BO) method, which models the objective function stochastically and intelligently selects the most promising hyperparameter configurations to identify the hyperparameter vector that maximizes the objective function. The Adam optimizer was implemented to address gradient descent resource issues and improve the speed of convergence with a learning rate of 0.001. We introduced Shapley Additive Explanations (XAI) to ensure security decisions are transparent, a key advantage over existing black-box approaches that helps meet ethical guidelines such as HIPAA and GDPR. The framework was evaluated on the Washington University in St. Louis Enhanced Healthcare Monitoring System (WUSTL-EHMS), as well as the new CIC-IoMT2024 (IoMT-specific) and BoT-IoT (general IoT) benchmark datasets. The results show strong detection capabilities, with high detection rates for critical attack types such as DoS with 99.94%, DoS SYN with 100%, and DoS TCP with 100%. The model also demonstrated exceptionally high precision for classes like DoS SYN, DDoS TCP, and ARP spoofing. Our proposed federated recurrent short-term memory framework achieves a robust balance between detection fidelity and computational efficiency, making it a reliable solution for intrusion detection in resource-constrained IoMT infrastructures.

title: ZimaBlue: Evolving Generalizable World Action Models through Scalable Video Pre-training
abstract: Robotic manipulation faces a fundamental scaling challenge: robust generalization demands broad physical experience, yet action-labeled robot trajectories are expensive to collect and inherently limited in diversity. Egocentric videos offer a far more scalable source of embodied experience, capturing object interactions, contact dynamics, tool use, and long-horizon behaviors across diverse environments. The central challenge is how to convert this abundant but action-free experience into effective robot control. We introduce ZimaBlue, a scalable framework for learning generalizable World Action Models (WAMs) from large-scale video. ZimaBlue follows a three-stage training curriculum: it first performs causal embodied video pre-training on large-scale human and robot egocentric videos, then grounds the learned visual dynamics in heterogeneous robot trajectories through video-action mid-training with a unified action representation, and finally specializes the model to a target robot for deployment. To make generative WAMs practical for real-time control, ZimaBluefurther adopts an asynchronous Slow-Fast dual-system architecture, where a high-capacity Slow world model provides generalizable spatiotemporal representations and a lightweight Fast branch enables 30 Hz action prediction on NVIDIA RTX 4090. On real-robot zero-shot evaluations, scaling from target-robot data alone to over 120,000 hours of embodied video improves success from 36.1% to 77.8%. ZimaBlue further delivers strong performance across multiple benchmarks, with particularly pronounced gains on unseen tasks.

title: Context-Aware Interleaved Batching for WhisperX
abstract: While WhisperX accelerates speech transcription via intra-audio batching, it isolates audio segments, losing the historical context needed for coherent punctuation and terminology transcription. Conversely, standard Whisper retains context sequentially but suffers from slow inference and hallucination loops. To achieve the best of both worlds, we propose Context-Aware Interleaved Batching. By using VAD-derived segment boundaries, our algorithm stabilizes Whisper's text conditioning, allowing us to safely maintain continuous historical context across batched audio segments. As demonstrated on long-form audio benchmarks, this approach reduces Word Error Rate (WER) and improves proper noun transcription, all while maintaining high-throughput inference speeds.

title: Multifidelity Computer Model Emulation Via Diffusion Model Steering and Targeted Maximum Likelihood
abstract: We develop a multifidelity method for fusing low-resolution simulations with computationally expensive high-resolution simulations, which are run infrequently and are therefore prone to bias. We formulate this fusion as a constrained optimization under missing-not-at-random (MNAR) selection bias. This formulation searches for the exponentially tilted high-resolution distribution that minimizes KL divergence from the biased baseline, subject to moment constraints derived from low-resolution simulations. This optimization requires first estimating the biased baseline conditional density $f$ as a nuisance parameter. We estimate $f$ using a score-based diffusion model. To eliminate the generative model's regularization bias that harms the downstream task, we apply targeted maximum likelihood estimation (TMLE). TMLE debiases $\hat{f}$ via a targeted exponential tilting, rendering the target parameters insensitive to first-order nuisance estimation errors. To execute this computationally, we adapt generative model steering, a technique originally developed for human-preference alignment. Using Feynman-Kac steering with a reward function based on our formulation, we simultaneously execute the exponential tilts for MNAR and TMLE at inference time, avoiding expensive retraining costs. Code available [here](https://github.com/Jong-Min-Moon/multifidel_emul_by_FK).

title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND ENANTIOSEMY: A PILOT EVALUATION OF LARGE LANGUAGE MODEL PERFORMANCE ON CONTRADICTORY WORD MEANINGS IN ENGLISH AND UZBEK
abstract: This article investigates the extent to which contemporary large language models (LLMs) correctly resolve enantiosemy - the phenomenon whereby a single lexical unit carries two opposite meanings within its semantic structure. Enantiosemy has been described extensively from structural, cognitive, and lexicographic perspectives, yet its treatment by artificial intelligence systems remains largely unexamined, particularly for typologically distant and comparatively lower-resource languages such as Uzbek. Combining a review of the theoretical literature with a small-scale diagnostic experiment, the study administered thirty-two disambiguating test sentences (sixteen English, sixteen Uzbek), each built around a lexical item capable of expressing opposite senses, to a general-purpose LLM (Claude, Anthropic, tested in July 2026). Responses were scored for sense accuracy and analysed qualitatively. The model resolved English enantiosemes with high accuracy (93.75%) when an explicit disambiguating co-text was present, but accuracy fell to 68.75% for Uzbek items, particularly those involving archaic, dialectal, or culturally bound senses, or requiring pragmatic and ironic inference rather than lexical co-text alone. The findings suggest that enantiosemy remains a genuine bottleneck for cross-linguistic natural language understanding and point to concrete directions for improving multilingual sense-disambiguation resources and evaluation benchmarks.

title: LM-IF : A Quest Driven Interactive Fiction Framework Using LLM
abstract: In this paper, we propose LM-IF, a framework that utilizes LLM as an engine for interactive fiction games. LM-IF generates a game world that is always playable from a game world setting document and allows the game to progress by interpreting commands freely entered by the player into sequences of actions. It provides players with consistent goals and narratives by presenting plot-driven quests as the primary criteria for memory updates and controlling their generation. LM-IF enables the creation and play of games using only the setting document without developer intervention, and allows for gameplay while maintaining long-term context despite the limitations of the standard model.

title: Self-Adaptive Geometric Field Theory for Quantum State Generation
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to quantum state generation leveraging the principles of self-adaptive geometric field theory. Traditional methods often rely on deterministic classical approaches, limiting the potential for nuanced and precisely controlled quantum states. We propose a framework that dynamically adjusts geometric parameters to mimic the evolution of quantum systems, offering unprecedented control and adaptability in generating specific quantum states. The core mechanism focuses on utilizing geometric fields to represent and evolve quantum states, enabling a fundamentally different approach to state creation. This research explores the potential of this technique to overcome limitations inherent in conventional quantum state generation, leading to new opportunities in quantum simulation and information processing. The investigation will detail the design of a self-adaptive geometric field theory, its implementation, and preliminary results demonstrating the capability to generate complex quantum states.

title: 基于多尺度信息流的量子隐形图的理论研究
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental quantum phenomenon, holds immense promise for revolutionizing computation and communication. This paper explores the theoretical foundations of a novel quantum information concept, termed "Multi-Scale Information Flow" (MSIF), and its potential application within quantum computing. We propose a model that leverages the inherent properties of information flow across multiple scales to enhance security and privacy. The core mechanism revolves around the integration of traditional information flow concepts with the MSIF, demonstrating its applicability and offering new quantum algorithms. The paper details the theoretical framework, explores potential benefits, and outlines a roadmap for future research and development.

title: Quantum Entanglement Self-Organization Modeling and Control
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, possesses unique properties that present significant challenges for practical implementation. This paper explores the concept of self-organization in quantum systems, focusing on modeling and controlling entanglement to achieve secure key distribution. We propose a novel framework utilizing a dynamically-controlled quantum network based on entanglement self-correlation to facilitate key sharing without the limitations imposed by classical communication channels. The core mechanism centers on leveraging this self-organization to create a robust and scalable protocol for secure quantum communication. This research delves into the mathematical foundations of this self-organization approach and demonstrates its potential for enhancing the security and efficiency of quantum key distribution.

title: Causal Inference with Time-Constant Networks
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to causal inference by leveraging the capabilities of Time-Constant Networks (TCNs). Traditional TCNs excel at capturing temporal dependencies within time series data, but they lack inherent mechanisms for discerning causal relationships from mere correlations. This research proposes integrating causal constraints directly into the TCN architecture, enabling the network to learn and reason about causal mechanisms. The core of the method involves introducing constraints within the convolutional layers of a TCN to mitigate the influence of future information, effectively mimicking the principles of causal inference. Combined with a suitable causal inference algorithm, this approach facilitates both model training and accurate predictions. The paper details the methodology, highlighting the unique advantages of utilizing TCNs' local receptive fields and long-range dependencies for causal relationship learning. We demonstrate the potential of this technique through a conceptual framework, aiming to establish a foundational approach for future research in causal time series modeling. ---

title: Quantum Topologies: Non-Linear Geometry Optimization
abstract: Quantum Topologies, a rapidly developing field of research, explores the use of quantum mechanics to model and optimize complex geometric shapes. This paper investigates the application of quantum topology constraints to solve problems with intricate geometric requirements, aiming to overcome limitations inherent in classical optimization techniques. We propose a novel algorithm – Quantum Topologies Constrained Optimization (QTO) – that utilizes quantum topology to guide the optimization process, enhancing solution quality and efficiency. The core mechanism centers around the inherent non-linearity of topology, which allows for novel exploration of the solution space, potentially leading to more effective and robust optimization. The paper presents a detailed theoretical framework and a practical implementation demonstrating the effectiveness of QTO in solving challenging geometric constraints.

title: ## Black-and-Red Bush Squirrel: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Foraging Behavior
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Black-and-Red Bush Squirrel" (BRBS), inspired by the foraging behavior of bush squirrels. These animals exhibit a unique strategy of alternating between searching for black and red food sources, demonstrating a dynamic exploration-exploitation balance. The BRBS algorithm leverages this behavior to optimize complex problems. The core of the algorithm centers around a dynamic population of agents, each representing a squirrel. Each agent possesses two distinct "searching modes": a "black mode" focused on exploiting current knowledge and a "red mode" focused on exploratory searching. The probability of transitioning between these modes is governed by a sigmoid function influenced by the current population density and the objective function value. Furthermore, a "cache" mechanism is implemented, mimicking the squirrel's ability to remember favored food locations. This cache influences the agent's decision to revisit previously successful areas. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and competitive results against established metaheuristic methods. The key parameters of the BRBS algorithm are: population size (N), black mode probability (p_b), red mode probability (p_r), cache size (C), and cache decay rate (α). The algorithm's objective is to minimize the objective function, denoted as f(x), where x represents the solution vector. The algorithm iteratively updates the solution set through the alternating searching modes and cache utilization, aiming to converge to the global optimum.

title: Black Squirrel Monkey-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (BSMMA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Black Squirrel Monkey-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (BSMMA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm designed to leverage the observed cognitive flexibility and adaptive behavior of black squirrel monkeys. The algorithm draws inspiration from their unique ability to rapidly adjust foraging strategies and problem-solving approaches in response to changing environmental conditions. BSMMA incorporates a dynamic adaptation mechanism based on reinforcement learning principles, mimicking the monkey's learning process. Specifically, the algorithm utilizes a 'contextual reward' system, where the reward associated with a solution depends on both its fitness and the current state of the search space. This contextual reward is dynamically adjusted based on a stochastic gradient derived from the solution's performance and a representation of the surrounding search landscape. The algorithm's core components include a population of candidate solutions, a dynamic adaptation rate, and a contextual reward function. We present a detailed description of the BSMMA, outlining its key features and operational principles. The algorithm's performance is demonstrated through simulations on several benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its ability to effectively explore complex search spaces and converge to optimal or near-optimal solutions. The results indicate that BSMMA exhibits competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms, particularly in scenarios requiring adaptability and rapid response to changing conditions. Future research directions include exploring the integration of more sophisticated reinforcement learning techniques and extending the algorithm to handle multi-objective optimization problems.

title: 基于生物神经网络的分布式时间序列预测
abstract: This paper investigates a novel approach to time series prediction by leveraging the principles of biological neural networks. Traditional deep learning methods often struggle with the inherent complexities and non-linearities present in real-world time series data. We propose a framework utilizing Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) with localized connections and synaptic plasticity, mimicking the architecture and dynamics of biological systems. The core mechanism involves adapting the synaptic weights within the SNN based on the input time series data itself, effectively learning temporal dependencies and patterns. We demonstrate that this biologically-inspired approach can achieve superior prediction accuracy and robustness compared to conventional methods, particularly for complex and noisy time series. The key innovation lies in moving away from the standard deep learning paradigm toward a system more closely aligned with the computational mechanisms observed in the brain. The results highlight the potential of bio-inspired models for tackling challenging prediction problems.

title: Cognitive Architectures for Robotic Embodiment
abstract: This paper explores the application of cognitive architectures to robotic embodiment, arguing that current robotic control systems are fundamentally limited by a lack of general-purpose intelligence. The core proposition is that integrating established cognitive architectures, such as ACT-R or Soar, into robotic platforms offers a pathway to creating robots capable of learning and adapting to previously unseen environments and tasks. This approach seeks to mimic the human cognitive process, enabling robots to exhibit more nuanced and flexible behavior. The presented framework details the implementation strategy, focusing on the architecture's key components and their integration with robotic actuators and sensors. We outline a methodology for mapping cognitive processes onto robotic actions, emphasizing the potential for creating robots with enhanced adaptability and intelligence. The research addresses the critical need for robotic systems that can operate effectively in dynamic and unpredictable real-world scenarios. This paper highlights the theoretical underpinnings and practical considerations for utilizing cognitive architectures as a foundation for truly intelligent robotic embodiment.

title: Algorithmic Self-Organization with Dynamic Network Topology
abstract: This paper explores the application of a genetic algorithm to generate complex, self-organizing patterns from dynamic network topology. Traditional approaches often rely on predefined rules or external prompting, limiting the potential for truly novel and emergent structures. Our work proposes a novel algorithm that iteratively modifies network connectivity driven by the input data's inherent properties, fostering a process of self-assembly leading to complex patterns. We demonstrate the algorithm's ability to produce structures that exhibit significant complexity and diversity, offering a significant advancement in algorithmic self-organization.

title: Behn's Bat: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Bat Foraging Behavior
abstract: This paper presents Behn's Bat, a new metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of bats. The algorithm mimics the bats' ability to efficiently search for food in a dynamic environment by incorporating key characteristics such as pulse-rate modulation, flight direction adjustment, and home-site selection. Behn's Bat utilizes a novel approach to population management and parameter adaptation, aiming to improve convergence speed and solution quality compared to existing metaheuristic methods. The algorithm employs a circular representation of the search space, a dynamic pulse-rate mechanism, and a probabilistic flight direction adjustment strategy. Performance evaluations on a range of benchmark optimization problems demonstrate that Behn's Bat exhibits competitive results, showcasing its potential as a robust and efficient metaheuristic. The algorithm's design focuses on adaptability and exploration, leading to effective solutions in complex optimization landscapes. Future research will explore the algorithm's application in various domains and its integration with other optimization techniques.

title: Core Claim: Develop a self-adaptive encoder capable of dynamically adjusting encoding parameters based on input data characteristics, enabling precise modeling of data distributions.
abstract: The field of machine learning has witnessed a growing emphasis on robust and adaptable models, particularly in the context of complex data distributions. This paper presents a novel self-adaptive encoder architecture designed to address this challenge. The core innovation lies in the ability of the encoder to dynamically adjust its encoding parameters based on the input data's inherent characteristics. This dynamic adjustment allows for a more refined and accurate representation of the data, leading to improved model performance and generalization capabilities. The proposed encoder leverages a sophisticated mechanism to capture data features, effectively transforming them into a set of potential vectors. The resulting mapping process enhances the encoder's capacity to represent and predict data distributions, offering a significant advancement in the design of adaptive learning models. This research contributes to the ongoing effort of creating more versatile and effective machine learning algorithms.

title: Geometric Phase Transitions for Machine Learning
abstract: This paper explores the application of geometric phase transitions to enhance the robustness and generalization capabilities of neural networks. Traditional neural networks suffer from sensitivity to initial conditions and require extensive hyperparameter tuning. We propose a novel algorithm that dynamically adjusts the network's parameters based on input data, effectively transitioning between distinct geometric phases of the network. This shift mitigates the effects of initial conditions and allows for better generalization across diverse datasets. The proposed method leverages a 'geometric phase map' to orchestrate the transitions, fostering more stable and adaptable learning. The core mechanism involves analyzing input data to identify relevant geometric phases, adjusting network parameters to stabilize these phases, and then transitioning between them. We demonstrate the efficacy of this approach through simulations and preliminary experiments on a simplified neural network architecture.

title: Graph-Based Representation of Linguistic Semantics
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to representing linguistic semantics by leveraging graph structures. The core idea is that semantic relationships between linguistic units – words, phrases, and concepts – can be effectively modeled and analyzed through graph-based representations. We introduce a framework where nodes represent these linguistic units, and edges signify the semantic connections between them, such as synonymy, antonymy, or hypernymy. This graph-based approach facilitates semantic traversal and analysis, potentially leading to significant improvements in natural language understanding and generation tasks. The representation allows for complex semantic relationships to be captured and manipulated, offering a more robust and flexible alternative to traditional symbolic approaches. This work lays the foundation for future research exploring the application of graph neural networks and other graph-based techniques in the field of linguistics and artificial intelligence.

title: Barbary Ground Squirrel Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the Barbary Ground Squirrel Algorithm (BGA), inspired by the foraging behavior of the Barbary ground squirrel. The BGA leverages the squirrel's efficient search strategy for food resources in a dynamic environment to solve complex optimization problems. The algorithm incorporates key elements of the squirrel's behavior, including territory marking, resource assessment, and adaptive movement patterns. Specifically, the BGA employs a modified particle swarm optimization (PSO) core, where particles represent potential solutions, and their movement is governed by a territory marking system that dynamically adjusts based on the perceived quality of the surrounding landscape. The algorithm's parameters are calibrated to mimic the squirrel's observed foraging habits. The performance of the BGA is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding near-optimal solutions within reasonable computation times. The results indicate that the BGA exhibits competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms, particularly in problems with high dimensionality and complex constraints. This research contributes to the field of metaheuristic optimization by presenting a biologically inspired approach that offers potential advantages in solving challenging real-world problems. title: Banner-tailed Kangaroo Rat Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm, termed the Banner-tailed Kangaroo Rat Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (BKR-MHOA), inspired by the foraging behavior of the banner-tailed kangaroo rat (Dipodomys spectabilis). These rodents exhibit remarkable efficiency in locating and exploiting scarce food resources in challenging environments. The algorithm leverages key aspects of their navigation strategy, including path planning, memory utilization, and adaptive movement patterns, to develop a robust optimization technique. The core of BKR-MHOA revolves around a modified version of the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) framework. We introduce three novel components: (1) a 'memory' mechanism mimicking the rat's recollection of previously visited food sources, (2) a 'direction adaptation' strategy based on the rat's turning angle adjustments, and (3) a 'resource scarcity' parameter to dynamically adjust the algorithm's exploration-exploitation balance. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a suite of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in achieving high solution quality and convergence speed. The results indicate that BKR-MHOA outperforms several established metaheuristic algorithms, particularly in complex, multi-dimensional search spaces. This research contributes to the field of metaheuristic optimization by offering a biologically inspired approach with demonstrated practical utility.

title: Graph Neural Networks with Adaptive Neighborhood Aggregation
abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have demonstrated remarkable success in various domains, including social network analysis, recommendation systems, and molecular property prediction. However, a key limitation of many GNN architectures lies in their static neighborhood aggregation strategy, often relying on fixed neighborhood sizes or simple averaging. This paper introduces a novel GNN architecture that addresses this limitation by dynamically adapting the size and composition of the neighborhood aggregation. We propose a mechanism where the network learns to selectively incorporate the most relevant neighbors for each node, guided by the node's features and the evolving graph structure. This adaptive approach enhances both the performance and generalization capabilities of the GNN, leading to improved accuracy and robustness. The core claim of this work is that dynamic adjustment of neighborhood aggregation significantly improves the effectiveness of GNNs. This work contributes to a more sophisticated and efficient utilization of GNNs for complex graph-structured data.

title: Information-Theoretic Robustness Evaluation for Neural Networks
abstract: This paper investigates a novel approach to evaluating the robustness of neural networks by leveraging information-theoretic measures. Traditional methods for assessing robustness often rely on adversarial example generation or direct sensitivity analysis, which can be computationally expensive and lack a fundamental understanding of how networks perceive uncertainty. We propose quantifying robustness through the mutual information between input features and network activations. This metric provides a direct measure of the network's sensitivity to input perturbations, reflecting the degree to which small changes in the input affect the network's output. Our framework offers a more principled and scalable method for assessing network vulnerability, moving beyond ad-hoc techniques and providing insights into the underlying mechanisms of robustness. The core of our approach lies in calculating the mutual information (MI) between input features (s1, s2, ..., sK) and network activations (a1, a2, ..., aL), where K is the number of input features and L is the number of network activations. This MI value represents the amount of information one variable (activations) reveals about another (input features). Higher MI values indicate greater sensitivity and, consequently, lower robustness. We demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of this approach through theoretical analysis and conceptual framework, outlining a methodology for quantifying robustness based on information flow within the network.

title: # Asia Minor Ground Squirrel Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the "Asia Minor Ground Squirrel Algorithm" (AMGSA), inspired by the foraging behavior of the Asia Minor Ground Squirrel (Sciurus anomalus). This algorithm leverages the squirrel's adaptive strategies for locating food resources – specifically its exploration, exploitation, and memory mechanisms – to effectively address complex optimization problems. AMGSA incorporates a unique adaptive parameter control mechanism based on the squirrel's responsiveness to environmental changes and food availability. The algorithm utilizes a population-based search strategy, incorporating a novel 'memory' component mimicking the squirrel's recollection of previously successful foraging locations. Mathematical formulations of the core components, including the position update, adaptive parameter adjustment, and memory update, are presented. The performance of AMGSA is evaluated through simulations on benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its competitive capabilities against established metaheuristic algorithms such as Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Genetic Algorithm (GA). The key contributions of this work lie in the innovative adaptation of the squirrel's foraging behavior into a robust and efficient metaheuristic framework. The algorithm's inherent adaptability and memory capabilities are expected to lead to improved performance in a wide range of optimization challenges.

title: Aroa Shrew Metaheuristic Algorithm (ASMA)
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, the Aroa Shrew Metaheuristic Algorithm (ASMA), inspired by the foraging behavior of the small-eared shrew (Aroa estivum). ASMA leverages the shrew's efficient exploration and exploitation strategies within a limited search space, mimicking its adaptive movement patterns and food selection. The algorithm incorporates a unique 'shrew-trail' mechanism, representing the memory of previously visited solutions, and a dynamic adaptation of the Lévy flight distribution to enhance exploration. We detail the algorithm's design, mathematical formulation, and demonstrate its effectiveness through simulations on benchmark optimization problems. The key contributions of ASMA lie in its adaptive trail memory and the dynamic Lévy flight, which improve convergence speed and solution quality compared to traditional metaheuristic approaches. Specifically, the algorithm's performance is evaluated using the following metrics: Function Value (F), Population Diversity (PD), and Convergence Rate (CR). The results demonstrate ASMA's potential for solving complex optimization problems efficiently.

title: ## Arizona Woodrat: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of *Neotoma pearsoni*
abstract: This paper proposes a new metaheuristic algorithm, Arizona Woodrat (AZR), inspired by the foraging strategies employed by the Arizona Woodrat (*Neotoma pearsoni*). The algorithm leverages the animal's adaptive exploration and exploitation of resources in a patchy environment to achieve efficient optimization. AZR combines elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) algorithms, introducing a novel 'patch awareness' mechanism and a dynamic population diversification strategy. The core innovation lies in the algorithm's ability to adaptively identify and prioritize resource-rich "patches" within the search space, mimicking the woodrat's tendency to focus on areas with higher food availability. Theoretical analysis demonstrates the algorithm's convergence properties and its potential for superior performance in complex optimization problems. Empirical testing across a range of benchmark functions reveals AZR's competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms, highlighting its effectiveness and adaptability.

title: Dynamic Topological Quantum Key Distribution
abstract: This paper explores the potential of utilizing dynamic topology in quantum key distribution (QKD) to enhance security. Traditional QKD protocols, reliant on quantum entanglement, can be vulnerable to eavesdropping. We propose a novel protocol that leverages the inherent dynamic properties of topological structures to create a more robust and secure key distribution system. The core mechanism involves dynamically adjusting the topology of the entangled state to detect and mitigate eavesdropping attempts. This research aims to address the limitations of current QKD methods and offers a promising path toward a more secure quantum communication infrastructure.

title: ## The Forest Cat Optimization Algorithm (FCoA): A Novel Metaheuristic for Complex Problem Solving
abstract: This paper introduces the Forest Cat Optimization Algorithm (FCoA), a novel metaheuristic inspired by the foraging strategies and spatial awareness of forest cat species, particularly the tiger cat. The algorithm leverages the tiger cat's ability to navigate complex environments, identify promising locations for food, and adapt its search strategy based on environmental feedback. FCoA incorporates elements of both particle swarm optimization (PSO) and simulated annealing (SA) to create a robust and adaptable search process. Specifically, the algorithm employs a 'territory' concept, mirroring the tiger cat's territorial behavior, and a 'resource density' metric to evaluate the desirability of potential solutions. The core innovation lies in the dynamic adjustment of the territory size and the frequency of temperature adjustments, both governed by a novel 'environmental fluctuation factor' derived from the observed seasonal changes in the tiger cat's habitat. This paper details the algorithm's theoretical framework, including the mathematical formulation of the key components, and presents a conceptual overview of its implementation. The aim is to demonstrate the potential of bio-inspired algorithms to address challenging optimization problems.

title: Dynamic Quantum Topological Network Routing
abstract: This paper investigates a novel routing mechanism for quantum information within dynamic topological networks, leveraging quantum entanglement and the inherent properties of topological networks. The core idea revolves around employing "quantum beacon" nodes, which utilize quantum entanglement to establish and maintain connections, and dynamically adjust the topology of the network to optimize quantum information routing. Traditional routing protocols rely on classical communication and shortest-path algorithms, which are inherently limited in the context of quantum information transfer due to the no-cloning theorem and the need for secure, state-preserving communication. This proposed approach bypasses these limitations by exploiting the unique characteristics of quantum networks. The system achieves dynamic routing by continuously calculating the optimal routing path based on the current network topology and quantum entanglement state, allowing for adaptability to changing conditions and improved performance. The paper details the theoretical framework, the mathematical model, and the core concepts underlying this dynamic routing strategy. We present a comprehensive analysis of the key parameters influencing the routing process and explore the potential benefits of this approach for building robust and efficient quantum communication networks.
