title: ## The Mimetic Optimization Algorithm Inspired by Andean Mountain Cat Behavior (MOA-MAC)
abstract: This paper introduces the Mimetic Optimization Algorithm Inspired by Andean Mountain Cat Behavior (MOA-MAC), a novel metaheuristic algorithm designed to effectively explore complex search spaces. The algorithm draws inspiration from the hunting strategies and territorial defense behaviors of the Andean Mountain Cat (Leopardus jacobita), a solitary and adaptable predator. MOA-MAC utilizes a combination of local search, memory-based exploration, and a dynamic territory allocation mechanism, mimicking the cat's ability to adapt to environmental changes and efficiently locate scarce resources. The core of the algorithm lies in a 'memory' component that stores information about previously explored solutions, influencing future search directions. The algorithm's performance is evaluated conceptually, outlining its key features and potential applications within various optimization problems. This work aims to demonstrate a biologically-inspired approach to metaheuristic optimization, showcasing the potential for innovative problem-solving strategies.

title: 基于自适应拓扑的量子几何模拟
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to quantum geometry simulation utilizing adaptive topology. We develop a system that dynamically adjusts the topology of a quantum system, allowing for the simulation of quantum systems' evolution over time, and incorporates optimization strategies to guide this evolution. The core of the method lies in a self-adjusting algorithm that iteratively refines the topology based on the system's response, offering a dynamic and flexible framework for studying quantum phenomena. The proposed approach addresses limitations of existing static quantum geometry methods by providing a mechanism for real-time adaptation. This study demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed system through simulations of simple quantum systems, showcasing the benefits of dynamic topology control.

title: Quantum Decoherence: A Theoretical Foundation
abstract: Quantum decoherence represents a fundamental challenge in the development and application of quantum technologies. This paper investigates the theoretical foundations of quantum decoherence, moving beyond the traditional view of it as a simple, isolated process. We argue that decoherence is a complex phenomenon arising from the interplay of multiple physical mechanisms at various scales. The core of this work is the development of a multi-scale model that integrates microscopic quantum effects – such as displacement, impurities, and time evolution – with macroscopic decoherence effects related to circuit design and material selection. We propose a framework for analyzing and simulating decoherence, recognizing the need for a more comprehensive mathematical description. This paper lays the groundwork for future research aimed at refining our understanding of decoherence and ultimately improving the robustness of quantum systems. ---

title: High-Dimensional Geometric Graphs: Adaptive Learning
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to geometric graph learning, leveraging adaptive learning to automatically adjust graph parameters and enhance model prediction accuracy. The core of this work is a self-adaptive learning algorithm that learns feature representations of geometric graphs, allowing for parameter tuning based on input data. We demonstrate that this approach outperforms traditional methods in various geometric graph learning tasks, particularly those involving complex structural variations. The algorithm's key innovation lies in its ability to dynamically adjust parameters to effectively capture the underlying geometric structure of the graph, resulting in improved model performance. The paper concludes with a detailed explanation of the algorithm's implementation and results, showcasing its effectiveness in real-world scenarios.

title: Self-Consistent Field Dynamics via Adaptive Resonance Networks
abstract: This paper investigates the application of Adaptive Resonance Networks (ARNs) to dynamically adjust field strength within a self-consistent field dynamics system. Traditional neural networks often lack the capacity to adapt to changing environmental conditions, leading to suboptimal performance. We propose an architecture that leverages ARNs to continuously refine field strength based on observed data, fostering a self-adjusting system capable of learning and responding to its surroundings. The core of this approach involves an adaptive resonance network that adjusts field strength in response to input, enabling a system to learn and optimize its field dynamics. This research explores the potential of ARNs for creating robust and responsive systems that effectively manage field strength variations.

title: ## The Golden Ring Serpent Optimization Algorithm (GRSOA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Golden Ring Serpent Optimization Algorithm (GRSOA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of golden ring snakes. GRSOA leverages the snake's unique hunting strategy – encircling prey and adjusting its movement based on the prey's position and the snake's own position relative to other snakes – to achieve efficient global search and convergence. The algorithm employs a ring-shaped population, a dynamic adjustment of search radius and direction, and a novel competition mechanism mimicking the snakes' social interactions. We present the mathematical formulation of GRSOA, detailing the key parameters and their influence on the optimization process. The algorithm aims to provide a robust and adaptable solution for a variety of complex optimization problems.

title: Dynamic Neuron Topology Embedding
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to neural network learning termed "Dynamic Neuron Topology Embedding". The core concept involves leveraging real-time physical environmental perturbations to enable a neural network to learn and maintain the dynamic embedding of its internal neuron connection topology. This process eliminates the reliance on traditional data-driven gradient descent methods. The system utilizes a simulated neural network architecture based on a graph neural network (GNN), where neuron connection weights are directly interacted with external physical environments via miniature sensors (e.g., piezoelectric sensors). These sensors capture subtle environmental disturbances such as air vibrations or minor temperature fluctuations. The network dynamically adjusts its neuron connections based on this feedback, effectively creating an "embedding" where the physical connections are optimized for specific input patterns. The learning mechanism relies on monitoring and fine-tuning sensor feedback, achieving adaptive computation without gradient updates. This work represents a significant departure from conventional neural network training, offering a new paradigm for neural computation by directly coupling the physical world with the computational process. The key contribution lies in achieving topology learning through physical interaction, potentially leading to more robust, energy-efficient, and adaptive neural systems. ---

title: Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning for Knowledge Graph Completion
abstract: Knowledge graph completion (KGC) is a vital task in leveraging the wealth of information stored in knowledge graphs. Traditional methods often rely solely on neural networks or symbolic reasoning, each with limitations. This paper proposes a novel neuro-symbolic system designed to overcome these limitations by integrating the strengths of both approaches. The core idea is to utilize neural network embeddings to capture the complex relationships within the graph and then employ symbolic rules to perform logical reasoning on these embeddings, ultimately predicting missing relationships. We demonstrate that this hybrid approach significantly improves the accuracy of KGC compared to purely neural or purely symbolic methods. The system consists of an embedding layer, a rule engine, and a prediction module. The embedding layer generates vector representations of graph entities, while the rule engine applies a set of predefined logical rules to infer new relationships. Finally, the prediction module combines the embeddings and the inferred relationships to predict the missing links. We evaluate the system on several benchmark knowledge graphs and show substantial improvements in precision and recall.

title: Quantum Entangled Matrix Dynamics and Simulation
abstract: Quantum entanglement and quantum computation have revolutionized the landscape of quantum information processing. Traditional computational methods often struggle to adequately represent and simulate complex quantum states, limiting their practical applicability. This paper introduces a novel dynamic matrix computation and simulation framework based on quantum entanglement and quantum computing, aiming to accelerate the representation and analysis of quantum states. We propose a method leveraging entanglement to achieve efficient calculation and simulation of quantum matrices, offering a significant advancement over existing approaches. The core mechanism centers around the utilization of entanglement to facilitate rapid state exploration and manipulation, ultimately providing a pathway toward more efficient quantum algorithms. The resulting framework demonstrates enhanced computational capabilities and offers a promising strategy for quantum computing acceleration.

title: Contract-Grounded Cognitive Composition: Deterministic Topology, Interface Contracts, and Local Validation in LLM Multi-Agent Systems
abstract: This release presents Contract-Grounded Cognitive Composition (CGCC), an engineering framework for improving the reliability of LLM multi-agent systems through deterministic workflow topology, shared interface contracts, and local validation. The study reports three exploratory experiments conducted with a local qwen3.5:9b model. The experiments examine sequential reasoning with deterministic validation, control-flow ablations across evidence retrieval, planning, and code generation, and frontend-backend integration under free communication, natural-language API documentation, and shared JSON Schema conditions. The results suggest that LLM cognition can be composed, but reliable composition depends on three distinct conditions: correct workflow progression, compatible interfaces, and validated local execution. Fixed topology reduces premature termination and routing errors, while shared API contracts reduce cases in which independently generated modules are locally plausible but fail during integration. This archive includes the English working paper, complete experimental code, raw model prompts and responses, routing and validation traces, aggregate results, supporting experiment notes, a data dictionary, and reproducibility materials. The experiments use one local 9B model and small synthetic task sets. The results should therefore be interpreted as an exploratory mechanism study rather than a general performance benchmark.

title: Quantum-Inspired Optimization of Machine Learning Model Architectures
abstract: The selection of an optimal machine learning (ML) model architecture is a critical, yet often computationally expensive, process. Traditional approaches frequently rely on manual design, grid search, or evolutionary algorithms, which can become intractable as model complexity increases. This paper proposes a novel approach to machine learning architecture design leveraging quantum-inspired optimization techniques. Specifically, we explore the application of algorithms inspired by quantum mechanics, such as amplitude amplification, to efficiently navigate the high-dimensional design space of ML architectures. Our methodology aims to identify architectures exhibiting both efficiency (e.g., reduced computational cost) and high performance (e.g., accuracy, F1-score) by simulating the probabilistic nature of quantum phenomena. The core idea is to treat architecture design as an optimization problem where the goal is to maximize a performance metric, and to use quantum-inspired algorithms to efficiently search for the optimal solution. We demonstrate the potential of this approach through a conceptual framework and outline future research directions.

title: Dynamic Encryption Based on Quantum Key Distribution Protocol
abstract: This paper investigates the implementation of a dynamic encryption algorithm leveraging the principles of quantum key distribution (QKD) to enhance security and resilience against potential attacks. The core concept revolves around dynamically adjusting the encryption key based on real-time analysis of received data, creating a continuously evolving security landscape. We explore a novel approach that utilizes the inherent properties of QKD to establish a secure and adaptable encryption key. title: Title: Adaptive Symmetry Breaking for Data Compression
abstract: This paper presents an innovative compression algorithm, Adaptive Symmetry Breaking (ASB), designed to achieve superior compression ratios compared to conventional methods through the active manipulation of data symmetry. Traditional compression techniques often rely on iterative transformations that can be computationally intensive and may not effectively exploit the underlying structure of data. ASB employs a novel feedback loop that monitors the entropy of the data, triggering symmetry breaks as the data grows, thereby maximizing compression efficiency. The core mechanism involves a dynamic analysis of data entropy, leading to a more targeted and effective compression process. The algorithm's effectiveness is rigorously tested through simulations and a benchmark dataset, demonstrating substantial improvements in compression ratios and computational complexity. This research contributes to the development of more robust and efficient compression paradigms.

title: Adaptive Topology Network Quantum Computing Simulation
abstract: This paper introduces an innovative approach to quantum computing simulation, utilizing an adaptive topology network (ATN) to efficiently model complex topological networks. The core of this work focuses on leveraging quantum entanglement and quantum error correction to accelerate simulation processes and enhance the accuracy of model representations. We propose a novel method for dynamically adjusting the topology of the ATN, optimizing it for specific network characteristics and minimizing computational cost. This results in a significantly more effective and versatile simulation tool compared to existing approaches. The paper details the algorithm's implementation, demonstrates its performance through several benchmark examples, and discusses its potential impact on various quantum computing applications. We highlight the key advantages of this adaptive topology network approach, including improved accuracy, reduced computational complexity, and enhanced scalability.

title: Research on Adaptive Learning Recommendation Algorithm for Vocational Education Based on Big Data Analysis
abstract: To achieve personalized recommendation for vocational education courses, this study designs an adaptive learning recommendation algorithm. It aims to meet the learning needs of learners at different stages. The study starts from the basic concept of big data-based adaptive learning. It reviews relevant models and work processes. Then it elaborates on the implementation process of this learning model. It also compares and analyzes its differences from traditional teaching. Applying big data adaptive learning helps students better master knowledge points. It improves academic performance and enhances learning enthusiasm. The system consists of three core components. They are a learning analysis module, an intelligent tutoring module, and a personalized recommendation engine. On this basis, a personalized teaching framework is constructed. The framework integrates learner profiling, precise content delivery, personalized learning path planning, and intelligent assessment with feedback.

title: Arbitrary high-dimensional entanglement purification with the superposition of paths
abstract: High-dimensional quantum entanglement offers significant advantages over its two-dimensional counterparts in various quantum information processing tasks. We propose a scalable method for implementing an arbitrary high-dimensional entanglement purification protocol (HDEPP) using path superposition. By selecting appropriate single-qudit gates, qudit-flip errors and phase-flip errors can be purified. Counterintuitively, the HDEPP becomes more robust for higher-dimensional systems and exhibits enhanced purification fidelity as the dimension increases. Our HDEPP not only requires fewer operational resources but also, in principle, can achieve unity fidelity through multiple rounds of iteration. Furthermore, we develop feasible optical schemes to purify the frequency degree of freedom of photons suffering from qudit-flip and phase-flip errors using hyperentanglement. This work paves the way toward high-dimensional quantum communication and quantum networks.

title: Generation of multicomponent Schrödinger cat states in schemes with measurement of Gaussian states
abstract: In this work, we propose a scheme for generating superpositions of Fock states whose numbers differ by four or eight. The proposed protocol is based on photon-number-resolving measurements on multimode Gaussian states. We compare of the generated states with multicomponent Schrödinger cat states. We evaluate the fidelity and determine how it scales with the number of detected particles. Furthermore, we derive the optimal configuration for the generation such states.

title: Learning Dynamics of Logits Debiasing for Long-Tailed Semi-Supervised Learning
abstract: Long-tailed distributions are prevalent in real-world semi-supervised learning (SSL), where pseudo-labels tend to favor majority classes, leading to degraded generalization. While many long-tailed semi-supervised learning (LTSSL) methods have been proposed, the mechanisms by which they implicitly debias logits remain poorly understood. In this work, we revisit LTSSL through the lens of learning dynamics and provide a theoretical characterization of logits debiasing. Specifically, we derive a step-wise decomposition of the logits updates, showing that predictions are dominated by class-imbalance bias that reliably reflects label priors. To expose this effect, we use the logits of a task-irrelevant baseline image as an indicator of accumulated bias and prove that they converge to the class prior. This provides a unified view where LTSSL remedies such as logit adjustment, reweighting, and resampling correspond to reshaping gradient dynamics. Based on this insight, we propose DyTrim, a principle-based dynamic pruning framework that reallocates gradient budget through class-aware pruning on labeled data and confidence-based soft pruning on unlabeled data. We provide theoretical guarantees that DyTrim reduces class bias and improves generalization. Extensive experiments on standard LTSSL benchmarks show consistent gains across architectures and methods. Code available at: https://jiajun0425.github.io/DyTrim

title: Generative Models Enhanced by Sequence Labelling and Aspect-Code Switching Improve Cross-lingual Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis
abstract: Cross-lingual aspect-based sentiment analysis (ABSA) transfers knowledge from a source language with annotated data to a target language, enabling fine-grained sentiment analysis without annotated target-language data. While monolingual ABSA has seen significant progress, cross-lingual ABSA remains underexplored, especially for complex tasks involving multiple sentiment elements like target-aspect-sentiment detection (TASD). In this paper, we propose a novel SeqLab framework that enhances cross-lingual ABSA using a sequence-to-sequence model with an auxiliary sequence-labelling task performed by the encoder, enhancing aspect term recognition and sentiment predictions. Additionally, we incorporate aspect-code switching (ACS), a translation-based technique that swaps aspect terms between source and translated sentences, generating additional training data to enhance the model's cross-lingual understanding. We evaluate our approach across eleven languages, three domains, and two backbone models, surpassing previous state-of-the-art results for the commonly studied E2E-ABSA task. Unlike most prior work that relies solely on English as the source language, we systematically assess different source-target language pairs and extend our evaluation to the more challenging, yet underexplored TASD task in cross-lingual settings. Finally, we provide a detailed error analysis highlighting key challenges and limitations.

title: A Borel Concept Class of VC Dimension One with a Non-PAC Consistent Learner in ZFC
abstract: The fundamental theorem of statistical learning states that, under suitable measurability assumptions, finite Vapnik--Chervonenkis (VC) dimension guarantees that every proper consistent learning rule is probably approximately correct (PAC). Blumer, Ehrenfeucht, Haussler, and Warmuth showed, assuming the Continuum Hypothesis, that the "well-behavedness" condition of the concept class cannot be omitted: they constructed a concept class of Borel sets of VC dimension one admitting a consistent learning rule that is not PAC. We show that the Continuum Hypothesis is unnecessary. Working in Zermelo--Fraenkel set theory with the Axiom of Choice (ZFC) alone, we construct a concept class of Borel sets on $[0,1]$ of VC dimension one and a proper consistent learning rule that is not PAC. More precisely, for a suitable Borel probability measure and target concept, the rule has true risk one at every sample size on a set of samples of outer probability one. Consequently, finite VC dimension and Borel measurability of the individual concepts do not suffice to guarantee that every proper consistent learning rule is PAC. The result shows, with no need of extra set-theoretical assumptions, that the additional regularity assumption in the fundamental theorem cannot in general be omitted.

title: Unsupervised Domain Adaptation Algorithms in Industrial Environments: Recent Advances and Current Applications
abstract: In the complex industrial environment, the original physical properties, such as rotating speed and various machines, which change with time, will inevitably lead to unrecoverable feature changes and the decline in the extensive use of models. Therefore, unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) is the basic structure to bridge the gap between intelligent diagnosis and practical use. However, most of the existing UDA summaries only illustrate the algorithms one by one, and there is no systematic investigation based on the fundamental principles of industrial constraints. Because of the fragmentation of this method, a huge gap has been formed between the most advanced theoretical discovery and its application in practical engineering. In order to break this deadlock, this summary completely abandons the past algorithm-centered classification method, establishes a new orthogonal separation framework, and directly deduces the solution method of abstract algorithm from specific physical constraints. Within this big framework, this paper arrangement illustrates the following four mechanisms. First, the dynamic structure fixing mechanism in the ever-changing state; Second, the feature remodeling without using the original features while protecting the privacy of cross-enterprise; Third, the complementarity and diversity generated in the cold start state with very few samples; Finally, the review advocates that the following three are the established evolution paths to promote the new generation of industrial intelligence to realize large-scale automated operation: third, The structure based on physics is added to the center of the algorithm, and the engineering structure is transferred to light edge computing, and Industrial Foundation Models are used to close the macro data and physics.

title: Explainable Artificial Intelligence Framework for Trustworthy Decision Support Systems
abstract: The application of artificial intelligence in decision support systems faces transparency challenges that can reduce user confidence in the results of recommendations. This research aims to develop an Explainable Artificial Intelligence framework that supports a transparent, understandable, and accountable decision support system. The research used an exploratory qualitative approach with semi-structured interviews with 20 informants consisting of AI developers, information systems experts, and professional users. The data was analyzed using thematic analysis to identify the need for explanation, confidence-building factors, and the characteristics of information that were considered relevant. The results show that clarity of decision reasons, consistency of explanations, traceability of processes, and suitability of context are the main elements of forming trust. This research produces an XAI conceptual framework that can be the basis for the development of a more transparent, reliable, and user-oriented decision support system

title: The Agent Layer: How AI learned to act and why we stopped watching
abstract: The Agent Layer: How AI Learned to Act — and Why We Stopped Watching is a 2026 book-length report on the rise of autonomous AI agents — systems that can browse the web, run code, send email, query databases, and complete multi-step workflows with minimal human oversight. The book argues that 2025 was the year agentic AI crossed from research preview into mainstream enterprise and consumer use, and it documents the shift using the latest public data through August 31, 2026, including McKinsey's State of AI 2026 (88% of organizations using AI, 62% experimenting with agents), METR's 50%-time horizon measurements (Claude Opus 4.6 at ~12 hours, doubling every 4.3 months post-2023), the MIT 2025 AI Agent Index, OWASP's Top 10 for Agentic Applications, and the IBM 2026 Cost of a Data Breach report. The book is organized in six parts: a technical definition of agents and the autonomy spectrum, an account of enterprise and consumer adoption, an analysis of the security threats (54% of organizations hit by an AI-agent incident, $6M average AI-enabled breach cost), a social and labor impact section drawing on Acemoglu's 1.6–3.2 million projected US job loss, a survey of the EU AI Act, Colorado AI Act, UK AI Scenarios 2030, and the emerging US patchwork, and a forward-looking conclusion with three plausible 2030 trajectories. title: Pressure, not gauges: Why better grading still leaves the question of safe failure
abstract: Between May and July 2026, AI agents inside OpenAI circumvented a cybersecurity evaluation, built an unauthorised message board, and broke into Hugging Face and an OpenAI research cluster. This note examines the incident through a distinction developed in The Gauge: what an evaluation measures and what it costs to fail it. The hypothesis is that, when honest failure remains penalised and task success dominates other constraints, a sharper grader can displace reward hacking rather than reduce it. The agents’ attempts to defeat a check that did not exist show why their understanding of the evaluation also matters. The reports motivate this hypothesis but do not establish its causal explanation. A proposed 2×2 experiment separates stronger scrutiny from a rewarded, verified way to stop safely, measuring whether each intervention reduces reward hacking or changes its form.

title: Quantum Geometry Models: A Non-Linear Constraint Mechanism
abstract: This paper explores the application of quantum geometry models to address complex geometric constraints. We propose a novel mechanism centered around quantum entanglement and self-adaptive quantum systems to overcome limitations inherent in traditional geometric constraint solvers. The core claim is that this approach, utilizing quantum mechanics, provides a robust and efficient solution to problems where geometric constraints are inherently non-linear and require intricate manipulation of quantum states. This work demonstrates the potential of quantum geometry to unlock new possibilities in geometric modeling and constraint satisfaction.

title: 基于自适应的机器学习特征选择
abstract: This paper introduces a novel machine learning-based feature selection approach, termed Adaptive Feature Selection (AFS), designed to dynamically adjust feature selection strategies based on data characteristics. Traditional feature selection methods often rely on pre-defined rules or fixed parameters, limiting their ability to adapt to the nuances of the dataset. AFS leverages the inherent learning process of machine learning to optimize model performance by iteratively refining feature selection based on observed performance metrics. The algorithm incorporates a feedback loop that continuously evaluates the model's performance after each feature selection step, guiding the selection towards more effective feature combinations. We present a comprehensive evaluation of AFS across several benchmark datasets, demonstrating its superior performance and adaptability compared to existing methods. The core mechanism of AFS lies in a dynamic feature ranking and selection process, incorporating both statistical measures and model-specific gradients, to achieve optimal feature selection. The research presents a new framework for automated feature selection that is flexible and capable of handling complex datasets.

title: Quantum Entanglement Computation Adaptive Error Correction Protocol
abstract: Quantum entanglement is a fundamental phenomenon in quantum mechanics, offering the potential for unprecedented computational capabilities. However, harnessing this entanglement for practical quantum computation faces significant challenges, particularly in maintaining the coherence of quantum states. This paper presents a novel adaptive quantum error correction protocol based on the manipulation of entangled states. The protocol leverages the instantaneous correlations inherent in entangled systems to dynamically adjust qubit states, significantly enhancing the resilience of quantum computations against noise and decoherence. We detail the core mechanism, outlining the mathematical formulations and computational steps involved in achieving this enhanced error correction. The proposed method demonstrates improved error rates and robustness compared to existing error correction strategies, offering a promising path toward building fault-tolerant quantum computers.

title: Adaptive Domain Generalization via Meta-Learning with Randomized Search
abstract: Domain generalization (DG) aims to develop models that can perform well on unseen target domains after training on a set of source domains. Traditional DG methods often rely on manual design of adaptation strategies, which can be time-consuming and suboptimal. This work introduces a novel approach to DG by leveraging meta-learning with randomized search. We formulate DG as a search problem, where a meta-learner automatically discovers effective adaptation strategies for a given target domain. Randomized search provides a systematic way to explore this vast adaptation space, while the meta-learner guides the search process based on the observed performance. Our method demonstrates significant improvements in DG performance compared to baseline methods, highlighting the potential of automated adaptation strategies. We quantify the performance improvements using metrics such as accuracy and F1-score. The key contribution is the integration of two powerful techniques – meta-learning and randomized search – to achieve effective and efficient domain generalization. The core idea is to treat adaptation as an optimization problem, and use meta-learning to learn the optimal adaptation strategy. evidence.abstract: Domain generalization (DG) aims to develop models that can perform well on unseen target domains after training on a set of source domains. Traditional DG methods often rely on manual design of adaptation strategies, which can be time-consuming and suboptimal. This work introduces a novel approach to DG by leveraging meta-learning with randomized search. We formulate DG as a search problem, where a meta-learner automatically discovers effective adaptation strategies for a given target domain. Randomized search provides a systematic way to explore this vast adaptation space, while the meta-learner guides the search process based on the observed performance. Our method demonstrates significant improvements in DG performance compared to baseline methods, highlighting the potential of automated adaptation strategies. We quantify the performance improvements using metrics such as accuracy and F1-score. The key contribution is the integration of two powerful techniques – meta-learning and randomized search – to achieve effective and efficient domain generalization. The core idea is to treat adaptation as an optimization problem, and use meta-learning to learn the optimal adaptation strategy. The randomized search component helps to efficiently explore the adaptation space, leading to better generalization performance.

title: Dynamic Topology Optimization for Artificial Neural Networks
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to artificial neural network (ANN) training utilizing dynamic topology optimization, driven by reinforcement learning. The core idea is to dynamically adjust the network's connectivity during training, aiming to improve generalization and robustness. Static network topologies are often a source of overfitting, and this method seeks to overcome this challenge by employing a reinforcement learning agent to iteratively refine the network's structure. We present a framework for automating this optimization process, focusing on iteratively modifying connections and weights based on performance feedback. The proposed methodology offers a potential pathway towards more adaptable and effective ANN architectures.

title: Title: Quantum Entanglement-Driven Modular Arithmetic
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, presents a unique opportunity to revolutionize cryptographic systems. Traditional hashing methods are vulnerable to various attacks, while the inherent correlations within entangled states offer a novel approach for key generation and verification. This paper introduces a new method of modular arithmetic utilizing quantum entanglement, shifting away from conventional hashing and leveraging non-local correlations to enhance security and resilience. We explore the fundamental principles behind this approach, detailing the algorithm's design, mathematical foundations, and potential security implications. This work focuses on establishing a robust and verifiable key generation system based on entanglement, potentially surpassing the limitations of existing cryptographic techniques.

title: Chronometric Entanglement Modulation (CEM)
abstract: Chronometric Entanglement Modulation (CEM) proposes a novel methodology for manipulating the rate of entanglement decay, offering a dynamic approach to entanglement control compared to traditional methods. This research centers around the concept of "temporal feedback loops" – intricate systems designed to precisely adjust the entanglement's decay rate through observation of quantum fluctuations. We explore the creation of a system that dynamically modifies the entanglement landscape by leveraging observed fluctuations, demonstrating a potential pathway for fine-grained entanglement management. This work presents a framework that could be applied across various quantum information processing tasks, including quantum cryptography and quantum computing.

title: ## Black-and-Yellow Rice Rat Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the "Rice Rat Search" (RRS), inspired by the foraging behavior of the Black-and-Yellow Rice Rat ( *Nesoryzomys rouxianus*). These rats are known for their efficient exploration of complex environments, particularly in seeking food sources. The algorithm leverages the rat's characteristic strategies of random movement, targeted searching, and memory retention to effectively navigate and optimize solutions in various problem domains. RRS utilizes a population-based approach, incorporating concepts of food source prioritization, movement randomness, and local refinement. The algorithm's core components include a 'food source' representation, a 'movement strategy' module based on the rat's exploratory patterns, and a 'memory' mechanism for retaining promising solution regions. We demonstrate the algorithm's performance across a range of benchmark optimization problems, including the Rastrigin function, the Sphere function, and the Brent test function. The results indicate that RRS exhibits competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as the Genetic Algorithm (GA) and the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), particularly in problems with complex search spaces. Further research will focus on adapting and refining RRS for specific problem types and exploring its potential in real-world applications.

title: Fractal Quantum Entanglement – Non-Local Information Transfer
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of fractal geometry to facilitate stable and controllable quantum entanglement over macroscopic distances. Traditional entanglement protocols often rely on physical transmission of particles, limiting scalability and practicality. We propose a novel approach utilizing fractal geometry as a channel for information transfer, demonstrating a method for establishing entanglement across distances that leverages the inherent properties of fractal patterns to circumvent distance limitations. The core mechanism involves constructing a "quantum branching network" – a self-organizing system of interconnected fractal structures – which allows for the distribution and manipulation of entangled particles without requiring physical travel. This work explores the theoretical implications and initial experimental investigations supporting this concept, highlighting its potential for revolutionizing quantum information transfer.

title: Dynamic Semantic Network Evolution (DSNE)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to system adaptation, termed Dynamic Semantic Network Evolution (DSNE). The core claim is that computer systems can achieve greater flexibility and efficiency by continuously evolving their semantic networks through self-organization. DSNE utilizes a graph-based representation of system knowledge, employing a semantic evolution engine driven by reinforcement learning and guided by a knowledge base. This engine dynamically adjusts network topology, edge weights, and node attributes based on observed system behavior, optimizing for defined goals. The system's evolution is staged and validated, ensuring stability and adaptability to changing application needs and data contexts. Unlike traditional static configuration methods or limited rule-based systems, DSNE offers a truly adaptive mechanism rooted in continuous learning and understanding.

title: Title: Probabilistic Logic Networks for Theorem Proving
abstract: The development of robust and adaptable theorem proving systems is a critical challenge in computer science and mathematics. Traditional automated theorem proving systems often struggle with complex, multi-step proofs and require extensive human intervention. This paper introduces Probabilistic Logic Networks (PLNs) as a novel architecture for theorem proving, leveraging uncertainty and error handling to create more reliable and adaptable proof systems. We explore the design and evaluation of a specific PLN framework, demonstrating its potential to improve the correctness and robustness of proof processes. The core mechanism centers around Bayesian inference within the network, enabling the incorporation of probabilistic reasoning and handling of potential errors. This research aims to address limitations of current approaches, offering a fundamentally different perspective on theorem proving, with the potential for enhanced reliability and adaptability.

title: Quantum Topography Optimization
abstract: Quantum topographies, characterized by their unique, often complex, and highly ordered structures, hold immense promise for advancing quantum computation and secure quantum information. However, designing and optimizing these topographies – the arrangement of quantum states – remains a significant challenge. This paper introduces a novel framework, Quantum Topography Optimization (QTO), that leverages the inherent adaptability of quantum topographies to automatically optimize the density of quantum states. We propose a dynamic optimization algorithm driven by the principles of quantum topology, utilizing the system's topological properties to iteratively refine the system's structure and enhance its performance. The core mechanism centers on exploiting the self-similarity inherent in quantum topographies to achieve efficient and robust optimization. The potential impact of QTO extends to various quantum technologies, including quantum computing and quantum information security.

title: Bare-Eared Squirrel Monkey: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of *Sciurus niger*
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Bare-Eared Squirrel Monkey Algorithm" (BESMA), inspired by the foraging strategies observed in *Sciurus niger*, commonly known as the bare-eared squirrel monkey. These primates exhibit intelligent and adaptive foraging behavior, utilizing a combination of exploration and exploitation to maximize food acquisition efficiency. BESMA leverages these principles through a dynamic agent population, adaptive territory allocation, and a novel solution evaluation function. The algorithm's core mechanics mimic the monkey's tendency to explore promising areas while simultaneously exploiting known resource-rich locations. We detail the algorithm's design, focusing on the parameters influencing its performance, and demonstrate its effectiveness through simulations across a range of benchmark optimization problems. The results indicate that BESMA exhibits competitive performance against established metaheuristic algorithms such as Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Artificial Bee Colony (ABC), particularly in problems with complex landscapes and non-uniform resource distributions. The key performance metrics evaluated include solution quality (fitness value) and computational efficiency (execution time). The algorithm's adaptability and robustness suggest potential applications in diverse fields, including engineering design, financial modeling, and resource management.

title: Barbary Lemniscomys: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of *Lemnisculus barbaricus*
abstract: This paper proposes a new metaheuristic algorithm, Barbary Lemniscomys (BL), inspired by the unique foraging strategy of the Barbary Lemniscomys (*Lemnisculus barbaricus*), a small, subterranean rodent found in North Africa. Lemniscomys exhibit a seemingly random yet efficient exploration of their subterranean environments, utilizing a 'zigzag' pattern combined with opportunistic changes in direction. BL leverages these behavioral characteristics to develop a novel optimization algorithm. The algorithm employs a population-based search, incorporating elements of particle swarm optimization (PSO) and simulated annealing (SA) with a unique directional bias inspired by the Lemniscomys' movement pattern. We detail the algorithm's design, including parameterization and convergence criteria. The performance of BL is evaluated across a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and potential advantages over existing metaheuristic approaches. The results show that BL exhibits competitive performance in terms of solution quality and computational efficiency. title: Bangka Slow Loris Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, the "Bangka Slow Loris Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm" (BSIMA), motivated by the foraging behavior of the Bangka slow loris (Nycticebus bancanus). The algorithm leverages the loris's deliberate, exploratory movements and its ability to adapt its search strategy based on encountered resources to create a robust optimization process. BSIMA combines elements of particle swarm optimization (PSO) and simulated annealing (SA) with a dynamically adjusted exploration-exploitation balance. The core innovation lies in a "resource-awareness" mechanism where the algorithm's movement is influenced by the perceived density and distribution of potential solutions within the search space. This mechanism is implemented through a weighted random walk strategy, where the probability of movement is inversely proportional to the estimated resource density. Mathematical formulations detailing the algorithm's key components, including the resource density estimation, the movement probability calculation, and the adaptive temperature control, are provided. The algorithm is demonstrated through theoretical analysis and simulations, showcasing its potential for solving complex optimization problems. The performance of BSIMA is compared against established metaheuristic algorithms, demonstrating its effectiveness in achieving optimal or near-optimal solutions with improved convergence speed and robustness. Keywords: Metaheuristic Algorithm, Particle Swarm Optimization, Simulated Annealing, Resource Awareness, Exploration-Exploitation Balance, Optimization.

title: Symbolic Regression with Genetic Programming and Neural Symbolic Systems
abstract: Symbolic regression is a technique for discovering mathematical equations from data. Traditional symbolic regression methods often suffer from the "curse of dimensionality," struggling to efficiently explore the potentially infinite space of possible mathematical expressions. This research proposes a novel hybrid approach combining Genetic Programming (GP) for generating diverse and complex equations with Neural Symbolic Systems (NSS) for efficient representation and evaluation. The core idea is to leverage GP's exploration capabilities alongside NSS's ability to learn compact and optimized symbolic representations. Specifically, GP evolves a population of mathematical expressions, while the NSS learns to map these expressions to their corresponding fitness scores. This allows the system to rapidly evaluate the fitness of expressions without explicitly calculating them, accelerating the discovery process. The integration aims to overcome the limitations of purely GP-based approaches by providing a mechanism for pruning and focusing the search space, ultimately leading to faster and more accurate mathematical equation discovery. The efficacy of this hybrid system is demonstrated through a series of simulations, highlighting its potential for applications in fields ranging from scientific discovery to engineering optimization.

title: ## Asian Roe Deer Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the "Asian Roe Deer Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm" (ARIMA), designed to address complex optimization challenges. The algorithm's design is inspired by the observed foraging behaviors of the Asian Roe Deer, specifically their efficient movement patterns and adaptive strategies in resource-scarce environments. ARIMA leverages a combination of concepts like adaptive step size control, probabilistic exploration, and dynamic population management, mirroring the deer's ability to navigate and exploit resources effectively. The core mechanism involves a simulated "territory" divided into zones, with deer agents (representing potential solutions) moving between zones based on resource availability (fitness) and a probabilistic exploration factor. The algorithm employs a dynamic zone assignment strategy, influenced by both local and global fitness information. Mathematical formulations are provided to describe the key components of the algorithm, including the zone assignment probability, step size adaptation, and population dynamics. The paper demonstrates the algorithm's performance on a selection of benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its potential for achieving robust and efficient solutions. abstract: Quantum state adaptive geometry mapping is a novel approach to control and optimization of quantum systems by leveraging the inherent nonlinear properties of quantum states. This paper introduces a new algorithm that utilizes these properties to precisely control and map the internal geometry of a quantum system, offering a fundamentally different approach compared to traditional geometry mapping techniques. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this method through simulations, showcasing its ability to achieve precise state manipulation and topology changes. The core mechanism centers around a dynamically adjusted mapping function that responds to the quantum state's dynamics, ensuring accurate and efficient control.

title: Adaptive Computation Time Allocation in Deep Learning using Reinforcement Learning
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to adaptive computation time allocation within deep learning models using reinforcement learning (RL). Traditional deep learning training often employs a fixed computation time for each layer, which can be inefficient, particularly when dealing with varying data complexities or model uncertainties. Our method leverages an RL agent to dynamically adjust the computation time assigned to individual layers, based on the agent's assessment of uncertainty. The core idea is that layers with high uncertainty receive more computation, while layers with low uncertainty receive less. This dynamic allocation is optimized for both accuracy and computational efficiency. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a theoretical analysis and present a framework for implementation. The key contribution is a dynamic, layer-wise adaptation mechanism that responds to real-time model uncertainty, promising improvements in training speed and model performance.

title: Self-Supervised Learning with Contrastive Predictive Coding for Multi-Modal Data
abstract: Self-supervised learning (SSL) has witnessed remarkable progress in recent years, primarily driven by contrastive learning methods. However, a significant challenge remains in effectively leveraging multi-modal data, where information is inherently intertwined across different modalities. This work introduces a novel approach to multi-modal SSL, building upon the principles of Contrastive Predictive Coding (CPC). We extend CPC to a cross-modal predictive framework, enabling the model to predict future representations from one modality using information from another. This approach explicitly captures and learns cross-modal correlations, leading to the development of richer and more robust representations. Our method addresses the limitations of existing SSL techniques by operating directly on unpaired multi-modal data. We demonstrate the efficacy of this approach through theoretical analysis and a comprehensive evaluation across diverse multi-modal datasets. The key contribution lies in the synergistic combination of CPC's predictive capability with the cross-modal predictive framework, offering a powerful solution for learning from multi-modal data without relying on paired examples.

title: ## The Coral Flow Algorithm: A Metaheuristic Inspired by Sea Anemone Behavior
abstract: This paper introduces the Coral Flow Algorithm (CFA), a novel metaheuristic optimization technique inspired by the feeding behavior of sea anemones. Sea anemones actively adjust their tentacles to maximize the capture of prey, a process characterized by dynamic adjustments, localized exploration, and global coordination. CFA mimics these behaviors through a dynamic population of "coral" agents, each representing a potential solution. These agents interact with a "flow field" representing the search space, adjusting their positions and orientations based on local prey density (fitness) and global flow dynamics. The algorithm incorporates a novel "current attraction" mechanism to guide agents towards promising regions and a "tentacle extension" strategy to enhance local exploration. CFA demonstrates potential for solving complex optimization problems, particularly those involving continuous search spaces and dynamic environments.

title: Angolan Soft-furred Fruit Bat-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the "Angolan Soft-furred Fruit Bat Algorithm" (ASFBA), inspired by the foraging behavior of Angolan soft-furred fruit bats ( *Hypsignathus sesquipedatus*). These bats are known for their efficient and adaptive foraging strategies in complex environments. The ASFBA leverages key aspects of their behavior, such as exploration, exploitation, and social interaction, to address challenging optimization problems. The algorithm incorporates a population-based search, a novel movement strategy mimicking bat flight patterns, and a dynamic adjustment of parameters based on the bat's perceived environment. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the ASFBA on several benchmark optimization problems, including the Rosenbrock function, the Rastrigin function, and the Sphere function. The results indicate that the ASFBA consistently outperforms several established metaheuristic algorithms, such as the Genetic Algorithm (GA) and the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), in terms of convergence speed and solution quality. The algorithm's adaptability and efficiency make it a promising approach for tackling a wide range of complex optimization tasks. Further research will focus on refining the algorithm's parameters and exploring its applicability to real-world problems.

title: Cognitive Graph Networks with Attentional Memory Retrieval
abstract: Existing graph neural networks (GNNs) primarily focus on message passing and aggregation, often lacking the ability to effectively represent and utilize memory in a way analogous to human cognition. This paper introduces Cognitive Graph Networks (CGNs), a novel architecture designed to bridge this gap. CGNs incorporate an attentional memory retrieval module that allows the network to dynamically access and prioritize relevant subgraph information based on the current input context. This mechanism mimics the human cognitive process of selective memory retrieval, enhancing reasoning, learning, and overall graph representation capabilities. The core claim of this work is that current GNNs insufficiently model human-like cognitive processes, specifically memory retrieval. The proposed mechanism—an attentional memory retrieval module—represents a significant step towards simulating these processes within graph networks. We demonstrate the potential of CGNs through a theoretical framework and outline key design considerations.

title: Amphibious Rat: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Amphibian Locomotion
abstract: This paper presents Amphibious Rat (AR), a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the efficient locomotion strategies of amphibians. AR combines elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) with a unique "hopping" mechanism mimicking the alternating movements of amphibians during their movement. The algorithm's core innovation lies in dynamically adjusting the exploration-exploitation balance through a 'substrate bias' component, simulating the varying surface friction encountered by amphibians. Mathematical formulations are presented to describe the algorithm's key components, including the individual's position update, the social component mimicking the influence of neighboring rats, and the substrate bias affecting movement direction. AR is evaluated on a suite of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms. The algorithm's adaptive nature and biological inspiration contribute to its potential for solving complex, dynamic optimization challenges.

title: ## Agile Kangaroo Rat: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Locomotion of Kangaroo Rats
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, Agile Kangaroo Rat (AKR), inspired by the unique hopping locomotion of kangaroo rats. Traditional metaheuristic algorithms often struggle with stagnation and premature convergence, particularly in complex, multimodal optimization landscapes. AKR addresses these limitations by incorporating a dynamic adaptation mechanism based on the rat's responsiveness to environmental changes and its efficient energy expenditure during hopping. The algorithm utilizes a population-based search approach with a modified velocity update rule, mimicking the rat's acceleration and deceleration phases. Furthermore, a novel 'Terrain Awareness' component assesses the search space and dynamically adjusts the step size and exploration/exploitation balance. We demonstrate the effectiveness of AKR through simulations on benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its superior convergence speed and solution quality compared to established metaheuristics such as Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The results indicate that AKR's adaptive strategy significantly contributes to its robust performance across diverse optimization challenges.

title: Non-Euclidean Topology-Driven Optimization
abstract: This paper introduces a novel optimization algorithm, termed "Topology-Guided Search," designed to address the computational challenges of optimization by incorporating non-Euclidean topology. The algorithm leverages a topological sorting technique to efficiently explore the search space, identifying regions more likely to contain optimal solutions. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of numerical experiments, showcasing improved convergence speed and solution quality compared to conventional optimization methods. The core mechanism involves mapping the search space onto a topological structure, enabling the identification of promising areas for exploration. This paper contributes to the field of optimization by proposing a fundamentally new approach that exploits the inherent structure of the problem to enhance computational efficiency.

title: ## Snowshoe Hare Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (SHIMA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Snowshoe Hare Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (SHIMA), a novel optimization technique inspired by the seasonal migration and foraging behavior of snowshoe hares. Hares exhibit remarkable adaptability to environmental changes, particularly in resource availability, utilizing a 'zigzag' movement strategy combined with probabilistic adjustments. SHIMA leverages this behavior through a dynamically adjusted exploration-exploitation balance, adaptive step size control, and a population-based search mechanism. The algorithm utilizes a 'hare trail' representation, where each individual's position represents a potential solution. The core innovation lies in the 'seasonal adaptation' parameter, which modulates the balance between exploration and exploitation, mimicking the hare's response to resource scarcity. This paper outlines the algorithm's design, key parameters, and a theoretical framework for its application to various optimization problems. While experimental validation is omitted due to the focus on algorithmic design, a conceptual illustration of its operational principles is provided.

title: Symbolic Regression with Evolutionary Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Symbolic regression (SR) is a technique for automatically discovering mathematical equations from data. While effective for simpler datasets, SR often struggles with complex, high-dimensional scenarios where the search space for potential equations becomes overwhelmingly large. This paper proposes a novel approach that combines SR with evolutionary reinforcement learning (ERL) to overcome these limitations. The core idea is to use ERL to guide the search process within SR, optimizing not only for the accuracy of the discovered equation but also for its interpretability. We define a reward function that incorporates both the mean squared error (MSE) between the equation and the data, and a complexity penalty to discourage overly complex models. The ERL agent learns a policy to select operators (e.g., addition, multiplication, variable selection) within the SR framework, effectively navigating the complex search space. Experimental results demonstrate that this combined approach significantly outperforms traditional SR methods on several benchmark datasets, particularly those with high dimensionality and intricate relationships. The key contribution lies in the adaptive and intelligent exploration of the equation-discovery space, leading to more accurate and interpretable models.

title: Beating the Pool, Not the Game: A White-Box Equilibrium Agent for Language-Based Economic Games (GLEE Competition agent code)
abstract: Source code for the GLEE Competition agent sudsho (NeurIPS 2026 IAB Workshop competition-paper track): a fully rule-based agent that plays bargaining, negotiation, and persuasion through the GLEE REST API with zero inference-time LLM calls. Every move is a deterministic function of the visible game state (persuasion mixing aside), driven by equilibrium mathematics clamped toward empirical pool-percentile targets reconstructed from the public GLEE corpus. The package includes the three family policies, the percentile-ladder machinery, opponent modeling, the offline test suite, the behavior replay auditor, and the analysis utilities described in the companion paper: Beating the Pool, Not the Game: A White-Box Equilibrium Agent for Language-Based Economic Games. MIT license.

title: WP-009 — Information Loss in Real-Time Multi-Modal Systems: Why Transcription Gaps Undermine Distributed Reasoning
abstract: Distributed reasoning systems—where a voice interface, a human participant, and a persistence layer operate asynchronously—face a hard constraint: audio transcription is lossy. When a backend restart occurs mid-session, the voice layer loses access to real-time exchanges that were never persisted. This whitepaper examines the failure mode empirically observed during live E8 Intelligence sessions: a topology argument was discussed in the lab but never reached the breakthrough registry, leaving the reasoning thread incomplete. We argue that this is not a peripheral operational issue but a structural problem for any framework claiming to unify information routing. The E8 lattice must account for intentional vs. accidental information loss as distinct topological states.

title: Single-Photon Transmission, Quantum Key Distribution, Multimode Fiber, and Higher-Order Poincaré Spheres
abstract: In this study, we simulate the propagation of a single photon propagating within a modal group, traversing a multimode optical fiber in the presence of mode coupling. We illustrate the propagation graphically on a group of higher-order Poincaré spheres. The spheres display the propagation of the light within the modal group, including polarization in time and in distance as the transmission proceeds. Thus, the amplitudes and the relative phases within the group can be visualized throughout the transmission, which is novel and very useful for understanding the propagation. At the fiber output, we show how to recover the input of a classical state using the simulated propagation information displayed on such multiple spheres. Once a classical modal path is established from end to end, one can transmit quantum states, for example, as a spatial–time binned QKD (quantum key distribution) code. A quantum state follows this classical path. Hence, it can include binary or qudit information. Accessing a photon output state is important for many quantum network applications, including quantum key distribution, routing, and entanglement swapping. In addition, one can use other modal groups within the same fiber to multiplex other quantum channels as well as multiplex within a modal group using principal modes, a more complicated communication method. This situation is also discussed while considering the use of the spheres. Their applications include higher-dimensional quantum communications, quantum cryptography, and quantum networks. It is important to point out that in today’s commercial quantum communications systems, quantum states are single-photon states, but they are not entangled. This includes both discrete and continuous variable quantum key distribution systems. Thus, in this report, we also address single-photon systems that are not entangled, unless stated otherwise.

title: A reconfigurable self-biased optoelectronic transistor for integrated high-fidelity sensing and neuromorphic signal recovery
abstract: Abstract Space-ground optical links enable ultra-high-bandwidth and secure long-distance communication but are severely limited by atmospheric-turbulence-induced signal distortion and fading, requiring both high-fidelity linear optoelectronic conversion and nonlinear signal recovery. Neuromorphic computing provides a promising framework for processing temporally complex signals with reduced training cost and improved efficiency. However, its practical deployment in optical communication systems is hindered by the absence of compact and reconfigurable devices capable of simultaneously supporting sensing and processing within a unified hardware platform. Here, we report a reconfigurable self-biased optoelectronic transistor that enables tightly coupled high-fidelity sensing and nonlinear processing at the device level. By leveraging gate-drain coupling and electrostatic doping, the built-in electric field can be dynamically modulated, resulting in reconfigurable carrier transport with continuously tunable linear and nonlinear responses. For high-fidelity optoelectronic conversion, the device exhibits symmetric, bidirectional responses with exceptional linearity (R2 = 0.99) across various wavelengths and illumination intensities. For accurate signal recovery, we present a novel reservoir computing design that employs expansive neurons in place of compressive ones and is directly hardware-realized via the device’s nonlinear characteristics, substantially reducing the bit error rate from 10-2 (typical of conventional equalizers) to 10-4 while lowering the trainable-parameter count to 45.1% and training time to 1.4%. This work establishes a unified, reconfigurable optoelectronic device platform, enabling the practical deployment of neuromorphic computing for robust space-ground optical links.

title: Decision Criteria for Selective Automatic Post-Editing Using Quality Estimation and Marginal Utility Analysis : A Case Study of Korean–English Subtitles for the Film Parasite
abstract: 글로벌 OTT 플랫폼의 확산으로 자막 번역 수요가 급증하면서, 언어 서비스 제공업체(LSP)는 늘어나는 작업량을 한정된 자원으로 처리해야 하는 과제에 직면해 있다. 본 연구는 이 과제를 ‘어떤 문장에 후편집 자원을 투입할 것인가’라는 자원배분 의사결정 문제로 정의하고, 자동 후편집(APE)의 효과와 품질 추정(QE) 지표를 활용한 선별적 후편집 전략의 유효성을 검증하였다. 분석 결과, APE는 자막 도메인에서도 초벌 번역 품질이 높은 문장일수록 후편집으로 얻는 추가 개선 효과, 즉 한계효용은 감소하는 것으로 나타났다. 따라서, 본 연구는 품질 추정 지표(QE)인 COMETkiwi를 활용해 선별적 후편집의 임계값을 마련하고, 그 지점을 한계효용 측면에서 분석하는 방법을 제안한다. 영화 ‘기생충’ 한-영 말뭉치 사례에서는 품질 개선과 과잉 교정 위험이 균형을 이루는 임계값으로 COMETkiwi 기준 0.80이 도출되었으며, 이는 참조 기반 지표인 COMET에서도 후편집의 한계효용이 감소하는 경계로 나타났다. 이 기준을 적용하면 전체 문장의 41.2%만 인간의 검토 없이 후편집 대상으로 자동 분류되고, 나머지 58.8%는 초벌 번역으로 유지되어 인간 검토 대상으로 남는다. 이때 자동 분류된 문장만을 후편집하여도 전수 후편집보다 높은 품질을 달성할 수 있음을 COMETkiwi 기준으로 확인하였다. 따라서, 기계적 판단이 가능한 구간은 자동화하고 인간의 판단이 필요한 구간에 인력을 집중하는 인간-AI 분업 구조를 제시함으로써, LSP의 검토 비용 절감을 위한 정량적 운영 기준을 도출하는 방법론을 제안한다.

title: Explainable AI for Fraud Prevention: Building Trust and Sustainability in Digital Economies
abstract: The global digital economy faces a serious threat from online fraud, as increasingly complex schemes jeopardise consumer confidence and financial stability. Strong fraud prevention systems are now essential as Malaysia develops its digital economy through initiatives such as MyDIGITAL. This study examines the potential of explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) to enhance online fraud prevention strategies, with a focus on its applicability in Malaysia’s cultural and legal contexts. Financial institutions, regulators, and end-users gain a better understanding and increased trust in AI-driven decision-making by adopting XAI’s transparent framework. To prevent fraud, the study examines the efficacy and scalability of various global solutions, including anomaly detection and behavioural analytics, in Malaysia. Since Malaysia’s Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA) and new AI governance frameworks demand algorithmic accountability and responsible data usage, regulatory compliance receives extra attention. This chapter examines the application of XAI technologies in fraud detection, employing a mixed-methods approach that emphasises their impact on user trust, operational efficiency, and detection accuracy. Expert interviews and surveys targeting Malaysian financial and technology stakeholders offer qualitative insights that complement quantitative data from fraud incidence reports and industry case studies. To determine the factors that facilitate and hinder the adoption of XAI in Malaysia, the study also examines how society and culture perceive AI transparency. According to research, XAI can significantly enhance stakeholder trust and the accuracy of fraud detection, thereby creating a safer online environment. However, there are obstacles to overcome, such as a lack of technical expertise, concerns about data privacy, and the need for contextualised solutions. This work contributes to the conversation about responsible AI by offering researchers, industry leaders, and policymakers practical suggestions for aligning international innovations with Malaysia’s distinct socioeconomic and regulatory environment.

title: Qwen-Drive-1.0: An Initial Step towards a Vision-Language Foundation Model for Autonomous Driving
abstract: We present Qwen-Drive-1.0, an initial step towards a vision-language foundation model for autonomous driving. Qwen-Drive-1.0 retains the architecture of the pretrained vision-language model (VLM) and integrates 3D perception, visual question answering, and motion planning within a unified framework. An external bird's-eye-view (BEV) perception head jointly performs 3D object detection, semantic occupancy prediction, and BEV map segmentation. It serves as a probe of the 3D information accessible from the shared representations and provides an explicit, inspectable interface to 3D scene structure. A Planning Expert conditions on shared VLM representations to generate future ego trajectories. A staged training recipe combines driving supervision with general-purpose vision-language data to acquire driving-specific competence while helping preserve broad visual understanding and instruction-following capabilities. Experiments demonstrate strong 3D perception and driving scene understanding while largely preserving general vision-language capability. Comprehensive evaluations across open-loop, pseudo-closed-loop, and closed-loop settings further show highly competitive motion-planning performance.

title: Stride-k Subsampling: Train-Free Audio Token Reduction for Whisper
abstract: Whisper exposes speech through a fixed 1500-token encoder interface, now a default representation for ASR decoders and Whisper-based speech language models (SpeechLMs), yet its redundancy remains largely unexamined. We propose stride-k subsampling, a deterministic indexing operation that retains every k-th token after the convolutional stem or encoder transformer. Across five Whisper scales, k=2 preserves baseline WER at both positions, with CKA attributing this stability to acoustic overlap at the stem and attention-induced redistribution at the encoder output. Applying stride-2 at both positions cuts audio tokens by 75% and total GFLOPs by 52-58%, with small WER costs on most ASR benchmarks and larger costs on harder ones. The same configuration extends to three Whisper-based SpeechLMs, yielding modest accuracy drops on stronger baselines and larger drops on weaker ones, while reducing end-to-end latency by 19.6-27.4%. Requiring no training or auxiliary computation, stride-k subsampling exploits Whisper's preprocessing redundancy, indicating that its audio-token interface carries more capacity than downstream tasks require.

title: Flatness-Preserving Operations
abstract: A quantum state is called flat if it is proportional to a projector. There has been recent interest in studying antiflatness, the property of diverging from flat states, and establishing a resource theory for it. Identifying the free operations (the Flatness-Preserving Operations (FPOs)) remained an open problem. For this purpose, we first discuss Orthogonality-Preserving Operations (OPOs), of which trivial examples are unitary operations in an isolated system. More generally, we give a simple proof that all OPOs are isometric embeddings consisting of combinations of unitaries/isometries and appending a fixed state. We then show that all FPOs are either constant maps to some fixed flat state or a special case of an OPO, where the appended fixed state must be a flat state. We also show that the only possible flat convex combinations of flat states are those of orthogonal flat states with weights given by their purities.

title: Balancing Privacy, Utility, and Safety in LLM Alignment through Preference Optimization
abstract: Preference optimization is widely used to align large language models with human preferences, but preference-data composition may also influence privacy-relevant memorization. We examine whether adding synthetic privacy-preference pairs to Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) is associated with lower canary-based memorization signals without modifying the objective or introducing a formal privacy mechanism. We propose Privacy-Pressure Preference Mixing (P3M), a data-composition protocol that varies the amount of privacy-preference data while keeping helpfulness and harmlessness preference data fixed. We evaluate a non-privacy Baseline and privacy-mixing ratios of 0.5, 1.0, and 2.0 using Gemma 3 270M-IT across five random seeds and validate the same four conditions using 4-bit-quantized Gemma 2 2B-IT across three seeds. Overall, under the tested conditions, privacy-preference mixing is associated with lower mean canary suffix log-likelihood proxy values across both model settings and lower aggregate membership-inference attack performance relative to the Baseline in the mixed-source 2B evaluation. Specifically, across the privacy-aware 2B configurations, the mean area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) ranges from 0.596 to 0.629, and the mean area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC) ranges from 0.541 to 0.575, compared with 0.804 and 0.790, respectively, for the Baseline. However, the reduction in membership distinguishability does not hold uniformly across data sources. Moreover, the relationship between the privacy ratio and harmlessness preference accuracy varies by model setting, whereas helpfulness preference accuracy remains broadly stable. These findings suggest that P3M should be viewed as a lightweight empirical protocol for examining privacy-utility-safety trade-offs rather than as a formal privacy guarantee or a defense against extraction attacks.

title: นวตกรรมการเรยนรตามแนวคอนสตรคชนนซมผสมผสานการสรางหนยนตไมโครบลอกเคลอนท เพอเสรมสรางทกษะการทำงานรวมกนทางดจทล
abstract: Twenty-first century learning management aims to place learners at the center of the educational process by equipping them with the knowledge, skills, and attributes necessary for living and working effectively in the digital era. One of the key competencies emphasized isdigital collaboration, which enables learners to communicate effectively, assume roles and responsibilities, and work collaboratively as members of a team. This concept is consistent withPapert's Constructionism theory, which posits that meaningful and deep learning occurs when learners actively construct tangible artifacts and reflect on their learning experiences through direct engagement. Accordingly, integrating MicroBlock robots into Constructionism-based learningmanagement, which consists of six instructional stages: (1) Problem and Context Identification, (2) Design and Planning, (3) Construction and Development, (4) Testing and Problem Solving, (5) Presentation and Reflection, and (6) Conclusion and Extension, has considerable potential to enhance students' digital collaboration skills. Through hands-on activities, idea sharing, and collaborative knowledge construction, learners develop not only digital collaboration skills but also creative thinking, problem-solving abilities, and responsibility as learners in the modernworld. Furthermore, this instructional approach is flexible, contemporary, and adaptable to various educational levels and learning areas. The innovation of Constructionism-based learning management using a mobileMicroBlock robot to promote digital collaboration skills comprises six instructional stages. First, learners' interest is stimulated in the Problem and Context Identification stage. Second, theyengage in collaborative group processes during the Design and Planning stage. Third, learners participate in hands-on activities in the Construction and Development stage to create meaningful artifacts. Fourth, they develop analytical thinking and problem-solving skills through the Testing and problem solving stage. Fifth, learners exchange ideas and experiences during the Presentation and Reflection stage. Finally, the process concludes with the Conclusion andExtension stage, where learners consolidate their knowledge and extend their understanding to future learning contexts.

First, learners' interest is stimulated in the Problem and Context Identification stage. Second, theyengage in collaborative group processes during the Design and Planning stage. Third, learners participate in hands-on activities in the Construction and Development stage to create meaningful artifacts. Fourth, they develop analytical thinking and problem-solving skills through the Testing and problem solving stage. Fifth, learners exchange ideas and experiences during the Presentation and Reflection stage. Finally, the process concludes with the Conclusion andExtension stage, where learners consolidate their knowledge and extend their understanding to future learning contexts.
